fields.title: MiR-326 targets ETS1 to activate PI3K/Akt signaling and promote malignant phenotypes in gastric cancer cells.
fields.description: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide and effective therapeutic targets remain limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the expression and functional role of miR-326 in gastric cancer, identify its direct target gene and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms involving the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and the regulation of inflammatory cytokines. METHODS: miR-326 expression was detected by qRT-PCR in 56 paired GC tissues and adjacent normal tissues, as well as in GC cell lines (SGC-7901, MKN-45, AGS) and normal GES-1 cells. CCK-8 assays, flow cytometry, Transwell migration/invasion assays and ELISA were performed to assess cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration/invasion and cytokine secretion. Dual-luciferase reporter assay and Western blotting were used to validate the target gene and pathway activation. RESULTS: miR-326 was significantly upregulated in GC tissues and cell lines. ETS1 was identified as a direct target of miR-326. Overexpression of miR-326 reduced ETS1 expression, activated the PI3K/Akt pathway (increased p-PI3K and p-AKT), promoted cell proliferation, migration and invasion, inhibited apoptosis and induced an imbalance of inflammatory cytokines (increased IL-6 and TNF-α; decreased IL-10 and IL-17). Co-overexpression of ETS1 or treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 reversed these effects. CONCLUSIONS: miR-326 promotes malignant phenotypes in gastric cancer cells by targeting ETS1, activating the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, and inducing dysregulation of inflammatory cytokines. The miR-326/ETS1/PI3K/Akt axis may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target for gastric cancer.

fields.title: Rast maqam and form in Azerbaijani âşık music: A modal–intonational analysis of selected airs from the epic "Âşık Garip"
fields.description: This study examines selected âşık airs performed within the epic Âşık Garip through a theoretical analysis of their modal–intonational, melodic, metro-rhythmic, and formal structures. Among the thirty-two airs constituting the narrative framework of the epic, fifteen are based on the Rast maqam; five representative examples- “Çukur Hava,” “Dastanı,” “Gülabi,” “Güllü Göyçe,” and “Kerem Köçtü”- were transcribed and analyzed in detail. The findings demonstrate that although these airs are grounded in the Rast maqam and particularly its Şikeste-i Fars section, their modal identity is dynamically articulated through shifting cadential tones, sectional expansion, and performance-based variation. The analyses reveal that recurring melodic nuclei -especially the “a” episode and its variants (a1, a2)- function as primary form-generating elements, ensuring structural coherence across multi-sectional designs. Metro-rhythmic organization plays a decisive role in shaping expressive character, often combining stable metric accompaniment with Ad libitum declamatory vocal delivery. Furthermore, the dialogic interaction between vocal and instrumental parts expands the harmonic and timbral field through saz-based quartal and quintal sonorities. Although the airs frequently appear in two- or three-sectional formal schemes, their underlying structural logic reflects a unified melodic core shaped by the semantic and narrative demands of the epic text. The study concludes that âşık music, as a syncretic oral art form integrating poetry and music, embodies structural flexibility, modal richness, and content-dependent formal variability within the framework of the Rast maqam tradition.

fields.title: Design, Fabrication, and Performance Evaluation of a Weeder for Upland Rice Production
fields.description: The weeding machine made of locally available materials using local manufacturing technology was designed, fabricated, and tested to evaluate its performance in terms of operating time, actual field capacity, field efficiency, weeding efficiency, percent damaged plants, and fuel consumption rate at different ranges of angular speed of the engine; three ranges of the engine’s angular speed (1501-2000 rpm; 2001-2500 rpm; and 2501-3000 rpm) were used. The experimental design was completely randomized design. The performance of the weeder was evaluated using three (3) to four (4) week-old rice plants. Results indicated that when the machine was operated at angular speed from 1501 to 3000 rpm will result in a mean operating time, actual field capacity, field efficiency, and fuel consumption rate of 155.23 seconds, 888.99 m2/hr, 74.53, and 0.75 L/hr, respectively. Further, the mean weeding efficiency is 88.42%, and the mean percent damaged plants is 0.46%. The weeding efficiency of the machine surpasses the minimum standard for weeding efficiency, and the percent damaged plants is lower than the maximum standard for percent damaged plants of 80% and 6%, respectively as specified in the Philippine National Standard (PNS) for weeders. When focusing mainly on manufacturing, assembling, and selling the machine, the investment model resulted in the following figures: Php14,601.69 net income per year, Php242,457.93 and 9 units break-even sales, 4.53 years payback period, and 18.07% return on investment. On the other hand, when considering machine rental as part of the investment model, the figures changed to Php28,266.29 net income per year, 5.92 ha break-even point, 0.59 years payback period, 1.69 benefit-cost ratio, and 169% return on investment. Additionally, a comparative performance evaluation between using a weeding machine and manual weeding revealed that using the machine resulted to an increased capacity and efficiency and a savings of Php4,840.00 in labor cost.

fields.title: A Study on the Cultural Resource Value Assessment of Min School Guqin and Cultural Creative Product Development Based on PEST Theory
fields.description: Taking the Min School (Pucheng School) Guqin as the research object, this paper designs a cultural resource value evaluation scale under the PEST theoretical framework, collects first-hand data via questionnaire survey, and performs descriptive statistics, reliability test, exploratory factor analysis and correlation analysis with SPSS to quantitatively evaluate the cultural resource value of the Min School Guqin. The study finds that the Min School Guqin has notable strengths in policy support and technology application, yet faces practical challenges including insufficiently unleashed market consumption demand and low audience participation. Based on empirical findings, this paper proposes targeted cultural and creative product development strategies from political, economic, social and technological dimensions, so as to provide practical references for the living inheritance and industrial development of the Min School Guqin, as well as methodological insights for value evaluation and development of similar intangible cultural heritage (ICH) resources.

fields.title: SOAR: Smooth Online Activation Routing for Stable Neural Learning from Evolving Streams
fields.description: Online neural learning requires models that update after each incoming example, remain calibrated under distributional change, and avoid brittle gradient transmission. The original version of this work used a small static benchmark, a shallow model, few random seeds, and no significance tests. This revision reformulates the problem as genuine prequential online learning and introduces Smooth Online Activation Routing (SOAR), a Hedge-style routing algorithm over smooth activation experts trained by singleinstance adaptive updates. SOAR links activation smoothness with online regret through a prediction-with-expert-advice bound: the mixture incurs only logarithmic-exponential-weight overhead relative to the best activation expert in hindsight, while each expert uses diagonal adaptive online gradients. We evaluate two-hidden-layer online neural networks on eight streams, fourteen methods, thirteen comparators, and eight random seeds, yielding 896 fully reproducible runs. The benchmark includes four real scikit-learn data sets and four synthetic streaming tasks with stationary, nonlinear, gradual-drift, and sudden-drift regimes. Across all dataset-seed blocks, SOAR obtains the best mean final accuracy ( $92.56 \%$ ), best mean negative log-likelihood ( 0.199 ), and best prequential accuracy ( $86.83 \%$ ). Paired Wilcoxon and Holm-corrected tests show significant improvements over ReLU, LeakyReLU, ELU, Softplus, Adam, SGD, and the compact ablation; improvements over the strongest fixed TeLU activation are positive but not statistically significant. The results support a nuanced conclusion: adaptive smooth activation routing is a robust online-learning mechanism and the best overall method in this controlled benchmark suite, but fixed smooth activations remain highly competitive on small static data.

fields.title: Routing, Summarization, and Memory in Neural Architectures For Reasoning and Language
fields.description: Scaling neural networks through larger models and longer context has enabled substantial improvements in their capabilities but has also dramatically increased their computational and memory costs. This dissertation develops methods for enabling efficient scaling using sparse models, context summarization and pruning, and neural memory. For model scaling, we study Mixture-of-Experts, where sparsity via routing allows scaling model size without a proportional increase in compute. We identify a limitation of standard Top-K routing, where unselected experts provide no gradients to the router, and introduce \emph{Default MoE} which provides a gradient signal for the unselected experts to learn better routing. For context scaling, we first study whether intermediate computations can be pruned from a reasoning LLM's context. \emph{Structured Thoughts} organizes reasoning into exploratory reasoning and their summaries. By training models to continue reasoning from summaries, we find that the exploratory reasoning can be pruned from the context, allowing models to perform extended reasoning while maintaining a shorter context. The second approach to efficient context scaling uses a memory mechanism with attention-based reads and writes, providing a flexible mechanism for storing and retrieving context. Our memory learns to solve several synthetic tasks requiring context storage and, when paired with local self-attention, enables language modeling that approaches the performance of full-attention Transformers in both pretraining and finetuning. We further investigate a hierarchical memory design with sparse access as a path towards scaling memory capacity efficiently.

fields.title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
fields.description: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

fields.title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Fashion and Apparel Related Reviews using Transformer Model
fields.description: The increasing reliance on e-commerce has led to a surge in customer-generated content, making sentiment analysis a crucial tool for understanding consumer preferences. This study presents a novel aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) approach to extract fine-grained insights from customer reviews across multiple product categories, including lingerie, women’s clothing, men’s clothing, kids’ apparel, home & furniture, and flowers & plants. We employ exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover key patterns in customer sentiment and utilize a transformer-based model with contrastive learning to enhance sentiment classification accuracy. Our approach effectively captures sentiment variations across nine different aspects, including quality, value for money, style, fit, material, warmth, comfort, support, and how well the product fits. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional sentiment analysis methods, offering a more structured understanding of customer feedback. By analyzing customer sentiments from reviews, businesses can identify dissatisfaction patterns that may contribute to customer churn. Addressing these issues proactively can help improve customer retention and loyalty. These insights can help businesses refine their product offerings and improve customer satisfaction across diverse e-commerce categories.

fields.title: Proposing Regression and Machine Learning Methods and Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average Time Series in Predicting the Price of Ripple Digital Currency
fields.description: This study proposes a hybrid forecasting approach for predicting the price of Ripple's digital currency, XRP, by integrating autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) time series models with machine learning (ML) techniques, including linear regression and ensemble methods. Leveraging historical price data, trading volume, market sentiment, and macroeconomic indicators, the hybrid model aims to capture both temporal dependencies and broader market dynamics for enhanced prediction accuracy. Continuous monitoring and adaptation are emphasized to address the dynamic nature of the cryptocurrency market. Accordingly, the methods of linear regression, support vector machine regression, decision tree regression, and random forest regression, as well as ARIMA, are used, which obtains the root mean squared error (RMSE) values of 0.9934, 0.9667, 0.9837, 0.9854, and 0.9178 respectively. Multiple regression is the most accurate model for predicting the value of the digital currency Ripple, whereas the ARIMA time series is the least accurate forecasting model. The novelty of the work lies in the heart of the accuracy of multiple regression in price prediction.

fields.title: STUDI SIMULASI DETEKSI EMAIL PHISHING BERBASIS NLP MENGGUNAKAN TF-IDF DENGAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE DAN RANDOM FOREST
fields.description: Phishing melalui email merupakan ancaman keamanan informasi yang memanfaatkan isi pesan untukmendorong pengguna memberikan informasi sensitif atau melakukan tindakan tertentu. Penelitian ini bertujuanmenganalisis kinerja Support Vector Machine (SVM) dan Random Forest pada klasifikasi email phishingberbasis Natural Language Processing (NLP) dengan representasi Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency(TF-IDF). Dataset simulasi awal berjumlah 10.420 email dan setelah pemeriksaan duplikasi, data kosong, sertalabel tidak valid diperoleh 10.000 email, yang terdiri atas 5.000 phishing dan 5.000 legitimate. Data diprosesmelalui cleaning, case folding, tokenization, dan stopword removal, kemudian ditransformasikan menjadi featurevector TF-IDF dengan unigram dan bigram. Dataset dibagi menggunakan rasio 80:20 untuk data training dantesting. Evaluasi model menggunakan confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil simulasimenunjukkan SVM memperoleh accuracy 96,40%, precision 95,94%, recall 96,90%, dan F1-score 96,42%,sedangkan Random Forest memperoleh accuracy 94,80%, precision 95,34%, recall 94,20%, dan F1-score94,77%. SVM juga menghasilkan false negative yang lebih rendah, yaitu 31 dibandingkan 58 pada RandomForest. Berdasarkan skenario simulasi, SVM menunjukkan kinerja lebih konsisten terutama pada recall dan F1-score, sehingga lebih sesuai sebagai model utama pada rancangan prototype deteksi email phishing. Hasil initetap perlu dikonfirmasi melalui eksperimen aktual dan pengujian lintas dataset sebelum digunakan sebagai dasarimplementasi operasional.

fields.title: Role of PANoptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic insights
fields.description: Abnormal cell death plays a crucial role in cancer development. Inducing tumor cell death is an important strategy for cancer treatment. Against this backdrop, with the in-depth study of the regulatory mechanisms of cell death, the discovery of interactions existing among pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis has resulted in the emergence of the concept of PANoptosis. This review article summarizes the discovery and molecular mechanisms of PANoptosis, as well as its roles in cancer development, tumor microenvironment regulation, and tumor metastasis, and explores its application prospects in cancer treatment. PANoptosis can promote anti-tumor immunity, but it has a dual-edged role in tumor metastasis. Targeted therapies against its key signaling molecules and combination therapies have shown promising results. For example, inhibiting the activity of ZBP1 can reduce the side effects of chemotherapy, and the combination of multiple molecules with radiotherapy or immunotherapy can enhance the therapeutic effect. However, in-depth research is still needed on the interaction and regulation mechanisms of its signaling pathways, as well as the activation mechanisms and functions of some molecules. Moreover, relevant targeted therapies and combination therapy regimens require more clinical trials for verification. In summary, PANoptosis provides a new perspective for tumor research and is expected to promote the development of precision medicine for tumors.

fields.title: iPSC neurodegenerative disease initiative isogenic CAG repeat iPSC line for Huntington's disease
fields.description: Purpose of Research: in the KOLF2.1J background as an additional disease series within the iPSC Neurodegenerative Disease Initiative (iNDI) collection. Major Findings: KO, were capable of differentiating to striatal and cortical neurons, astrocytes and microglia using established protocols. General quality control stains and morphological analyses are described for each differentiation. A selected set of assays were carried out on differentiated cells; expanded repeat expressing astrocytes showed altered expression of astrocyte protein markers and morphological characteristics, and striatal neurons showed altered DARPP-32/CTIP2 colocalization. mRNAseq carried out for striatal neurons showed high similarities in gene expression changes between 79Q and KO lines compared to the unexpanded repeat. Conclusions: The KOLF2.1J isogenic CAG repeat series serves as a community resource to study HD mechanisms with the potential for direct comparison across other neurodegenerative diseases through the iNDI collection.

fields.title: High-Throughput Screening of a Lipid Nanoparticle (LNP) Library Identifies Lead Formulations for CRISPR-Cas9 Ribonucleoprotein Delivery and Gene Editing
fields.description: Abstract Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) using synthetic materials can bypass the host translational machinery and limit the duration of genomic exposure, minimizing the risk of off-target mutations. Despite their advantages, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery that achieve highly efficient editing at low doses remain limited. In the present study, we developed a library of ionizable lipids (ILs) and corresponding LNPs to enhance the delivery and editing efficiencies of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complexes. Following comprehensive in vitro screening and formulation optimization, an optimal LNP candidate containing the C12A9 IL (denoted as LNPC12A9) was identified that achieved ∼90% EGFP disruption in HEK293T-EGFP cells at an RNP concentration of 30 nM and ∼60% at 15 nM. The editing performance was consistently observed at an RNP concentration of 15 nM when editing the Gcgr and HPRT1 genes across multiple hepatic cell lines. Moreover, coencapsulation of RNP and a single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (ssODN) template for homology-directed repair (HDR) within LNPC12A9 induced an HDR rate of 37.8%. Systemic administration of LNPC12A9 into C57BL/6J mice led to liver tropism and a total hepatic Pcsk9 gene disruption rate of 1.39%. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the construction of an LNP platform to improve the delivery efficiency of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP, thereby facilitating the development of LNPs for safe, precise, and tissue-specific Cas9 RNP-based genome editing therapies.

fields.title: Next-generation natural killer cell therapy: bench to bedside and beyond
fields.description: Natural killer (NK) cells have emerged as central players in cancer immunotherapy, progressing from basic discovery to clinically validated platforms over five decades. This review synthesizes the evolving understanding of NK cell biology, including subset heterogeneity, epigenetic regulation, and metabolic control, and, as innovative focal points, intratumoral NK heterogeneity, epigenetic modulation, and intracellular immune checkpoints, forming the foundation for rational therapeutic engineering. We examine the clinical trajectory from unmodified adoptive transfer to cytokine-induced memory-like NK cells and, most transformatively, to chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-NK cells. Landmark trials have established the remarkable efficacy and superior safety of CAR-NK cells in B-cell malignancies, with recent studies extending these benefits to autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis, demonstrating durable immune reset with a favorable safety profile. Despite these advances, solid tumors remain formidable challenges, hindered by antigen heterogeneity, physical barriers, and a metabolically hostile microenvironment. We therefore analyze next-generation engineering strategies that move beyond single modifications toward systems-level reprogramming, encompassing intrinsic enhancements (cytokine signaling, metabolic fitness, checkpoint disruption), extrinsic tumor microenvironment remodeling, and advanced delivery platforms. We further synthesize the practical dimensions of clinical translation by systematically examining key optimization parameters that will guide the path toward precision NK cell therapy. These include rational dosing and scheduling regimens, strategies to reduce lymphodepletion intensity, context-dependent persistence requirements across different disease indications and the emerging biomarker landscape.

fields.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease
fields.description: Retinal degenerative diseases, including age-related macular degeneration (AMD), retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people. Cell-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplantation, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long-term outcome monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and post-transplantation monitoring through multimodal retinal imaging. fields.title: Functional dissection of ultraconserved non-coding regions present near the Hoxd complex in vertebrates
fields.description: Ultraconserved non-coding elements (UCEs) exhibit near-perfect sequence conservation across vertebrate genomes, implying severe evolutionary constraint and essential biological functions. Near the vertebrate Hoxd complex, a master regulator of axial patterning and limb morphogenesis, three Conserved Regions (CR1, CR2, and CR3), each longer than 200 bp, show exceptional sequence conservation and drive robust regulatory activity in transient reporter assays. To investigate their endogenous in vivo functions, we used CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to generate a series of deletions of varying sizes spanning CR2 and CR3, individually and in combination, within hoxd complex in zebrafish. Screening thousands of founder embryos revealed a clear size and conservation-dependent relationship between deletion extent and viability: complete deletion of core CR2, CR3, or the combined CR2/3 loci could not be transmitted through the germline, whereas the smaller and least-conserved deletion, a 626-bp subregion of CR2, was the only allele to yield a stable, homozygous-viable line. Our results indicate that the core ultraconserved sequences are developmentally indispensable, whereas flanking, less conserved sequences can be removed without consequence. Detailed phenotypic and molecular characterization of the mutant embryos revealed normal primary and secondary body axis formation, intact somite segmentation, and unperturbed craniofacial and pectoral fin development. Expression of hoxd complex genes showed no significant change in mutant embryos by RNA-ISH or RT-qPCR, although RT-qPCR revealed a consistent, modest upward trend at 24 and 48 hpf, raising the possibility that the deleted subregion normally contributes a weak repression of overall hoxd complex genes transcription. While this study reveals some functional aspects of ultraconserved elements, much more remains to be uncovered.

fields.title: CRISPR/Cas9 induced disruption of oca2 and tyr genes associated with pigmentation in Danio rerio
fields.description: Targeted disruption of genes has been successfully carried out in several model and non-model fish species. In ornamental fish industries, Danio rerio (D. rerio) represents the most significant fish species and is available in several color varieties. Recently, CRISPR/Cas9 has been used to disrupt pigmented genes in several fish species, including D. rerio . However, there have been few reports on the use of CRISPR/Cas9 for the disruption of pigmented genes tyrosinase (tyr) and oculocutaneous albinism II ( oca2 ) in D. rerio to date. In this study, guide RNA (gRNA) constructs specific to the tyr (T1) and oca2 (T2) genes were designed and synthesized, while Cas9 mRNA was synthesized through in vitro transcription. Subsequently, both the Cas9 mRNA and the gRNA constructs were validated using gel electrophoresis and sequencing. The validated Cas9 mRNA and gRNA mixture was then co-microinjected into D. rerio embryos at the 1–2 cell stage, which were obtained through natural spawning and later reared under controlled conditions. The results of gel electrophoresis and sequencing confirmed the successful synthesis and validation of the T1 and T2 targeting Cas9 mRNA and gRNA constructs. Melanophores were reduced when the T1 and T2 genes were disrupted, according to phenotypic studies of the Fo and F1 mutants, leading to visible pigmentation alterations. Furthermore, the validated gene editing constructs developed in this study may serve as useful tools for targeted pigmentation modification in other ornamental fish species, thereby supporting the development of high-value ornamental strains and advancing genetic improvement programs in aquaculture. However, further studies are required at the molecular level to confirm the mutation by genotyping.

fields.title: Development of an Efficient In Vitro Propagation Protocol for the Elite Bidah Pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) Landrace in Saudi Arabia
fields.description: The Bidah pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) is an elite landrace native to Wadi Bidah in the Al-Baha region of Saudi Arabia. This cultivar is distinguished by its unique taste, high yield, genetic component, and phytochemical profile. In addition, its resilience to harsh environmental conditions aligns closely with national priorities in sustainable agriculture and food security. This study articulated the successful micropropagation of the Bidah pomegranate cultivar using both direct and indirect in vitro approaches. Phenolic exudation was effectively mitigated through sequential subculturing onto a plant growth regulator (PGR)-free medium. fields.title: HNRNPH2-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids
fields.description: Autism spectrum disorder has been linked to disrupted RNA processing during corticogenesis, yet variant-specific mechanisms remain difficult to resolve. Isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart serve as a human developmental model to investigate variant-associated RNA dysregulation. Imaging quantification and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing, performed at a single developmental time point on a pooled organoid RNA from each genotype, identify coordinated remodeling of neuronal and metabolic programs, along with junction-centered splicing dysregulation involving 6,310 differentially used junctions. Computational structural docking situates HNRNPH2 RNA recognition motifs (RRMs) 1–3 within a spliceosomal context and locates residue R114 near a predicted RNA-contact interface, indicating that the R114W substitution may alter RNA engagement. Integration of differential expression with event- and isoform-level analyses identifies regulatory hubs enriched for axon guidance and synaptic signaling pathways. Single-cell-reference-based deconvolution suggests modest compositional shifts that are unlikely to account for the extent of transcriptional and splicing alterations observed. Collectively, these findings imply HNRNPH2-R114W in widespread RNA rewiring and define candidate isoform-level endpoints for mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in human cortical organoids. These molecular signatures open new avenues to examine how HNRNPH2-associated RNA dysregulation evolves across developmental time and recurs across independent biological contexts, providing a foundation for further mechanistic studies of this rare neurodevelopmental disorder.

fields.title: VASP cooperates with zyxin to organize mechanically competent adhesions
fields.description: Abstract Focal adhesions (FAs) are dynamic macromolecular assemblies that anchor the actin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix via integrin receptors, thereby regulating cell morphology and migration. Here, we show that the vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP) cooperates with the mechanosensitive scaffold protein zyxin to maintain FA during maturation under actomyosin-generated tension. Using sequential CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing and cryo-electron tomography, we resolved the in situ nanoarchitecture of the FA-stress fiber interface. We establish that tropomyosin decorates the dorsal aspect of adhesion-associated stress fibers independently of VASP and zyxin. VASP and zyxin are required for the assembly of dense, aligned actin bundles with uniform polarity, oriented with their barbed ends toward the cell edge. Live-cell imaging and quantitative analyses of cells confined on micropatterns reveal that VASP and zyxin cooperate to preserve the mechanical coupling between FAs and the actin cytoskeleton under contractile load. Our findings establish that VASP and zyxin perform distinct yet complementary functions to organize FA-associated actin into mechanically competent force-transmitting units.

fields.title: Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
fields.description: Most characterized anti-CRISPR proteins act via well-defined core inhibitory mechanisms, yet how auxiliary structural elements modulate and potentiate these canonical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AcrIIC1Boe represses Nme1Cas9 activity through an integrated, loop-coupled regulatory mode. Based on canonical occlusion of the HNH catalytic site, the extended loop of AcrIIC1Boe provides an additional coupled regulatory layer to remodel sgRNA spacer arrangement and R-loop progression, thereby enhancing Cas9 inhibition. Loop deletion largely abrogates robust inhibition, indicating that this loop module is indispensable for full AcrIIC1 inhibitory potency. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1Nme1 efficiently elevates its inhibitory performance. Our findings identify a loop-mediated regulatory strategy that potentiates the canonical HNH occlusion mechanism, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence across AcrIIC1 homologs, and offer a modular engineering principle for the rational design and optimization of anti-CRISPR proteins with enhanced potency. Anti-CRISPR proteins inhibit bacterial CRISPR immunity, but how auxiliary structural elements enhance inhibition is unclear. Here, authors show that an extended AcrIIC1 loop supports HNH-domain engagement and modulates sgRNA positioning and R-loop formation to strengthen Cas9 inhibition.

fields.title: Volume X Synthesis: The Epistemological Arc, from Dual Clocks to Residual Risk (Slide Deck)
fields.description: This 14-slide deck synthesises the KSCCN Series Volumes III–X on quantum readiness, starting from the dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage clock and already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural clocks. It summarises quantum memory figures of merit, modular cryogenic interconnects (IBM, Bluefors), cryo-CMOS control electronics, and molecular entanglement entropy with fermionic superselection rules. It sets out four residual-risk readiness indicators, applies them to sovereign Global South pathways, two molecular systems (vinylene carbonate + singlet oxygen and iron–sulfur clusters/FeMo-cofactor) and 2027–2029 vendor roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Apollo). It concludes that usable capability is a vector of thresholds rather than a single predicted year, and that dual clocks continue to run independently of vendor milestones. Slide headings: 1. fields.title: Volume X: The Epistemological Arc: From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk, Molecular Entanglement and Sovereign Pathways
fields.description: This tenth volume narrates the epistemological and theoretical arc of the inquiry that began with a dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage timeline and an already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural-integration timeline. Successive volumes established quantum memory specifications, examined modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control as complementary solutions to scaling bottlenecks, quantified molecular entanglement entropy and the purifying effect of fermionic superselection rules, converted residual gaps into readiness indicators, and mapped those indicators onto sovereign pathways, concrete molecular systems and published 2027–2029 roadmaps. The arc demonstrates that usable quantum capability for molecular simulation and cryptographic relevance is governed by a vector of measurable thresholds—logical error, modular memory integration, cryo-CMOS power and superselection overhead—rather than by any single predicted year. The findings supply a practical, dual-clock framework for readiness that remains independent of vendor milestones.

fields.title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
fields.description: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

fields.title: Enhanced quantum parameter estimation based on the Hardy paradox
fields.description: Statistical paradoxes such as the Hardy paradox and the enhancement of phase estimation via post-selection both draw upon the same non-classical features of quantum statistics described by non-positive quasi-probabilities. In this paper, we introduce a post-selected quantum metrology scenario where the initial state, the dynamics associated with the phase shift, and the post-selection are all inspired by the Hardy paradox. Specifically, we identify an anomalous weak value that is characteristic of both the Hardy paradox and the potential enhancement of sensitivity by the post-selection. We find that the efficiency of the enhancement is reduced when the expectation value associated with the anomalous weak value is different from the inverse of this value. We conclude that the relation between enhanced phase estimation and the Hardy paradox requires a detailed understanding of the relation between weak values and expectation values.

fields.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
fields.description: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. fields.title: Subvacuum jamming for secure communication
fields.description: Artificial-noise jamming improves physical-layer security by degrading an eavesdropper's channel, but the injected noise also interferes with the legitimate receiver. We introduce a correlated-jamming protocol based on classical and quantum correlations that suppresses this self-interference while preserving the jamming penalty experienced by the eavesdropper. Bob broadcasts one mode of a correlated two-mode source and retains the second as a local reference. Eve, who has no access to the retained mode, receives the full thermal jamming field, whereas Bob uses an optimized joint measurement to cancel its correlated fluctuations. The residual self-jamming noise is governed by the conditional variance of the transmitted jamming quadrature given the retained reference. Any classically correlated source is bounded by the vacuum-noise floor and therefore restores Bob, at best, to his unjammed receiver noise. An entangled two-mode squeezed source surpasses this limit and produces sub-vacuum residual noise, with the maximum quantum advantage set by the transmissivity of the jamming path back to Bob. In the bright-source regime, this advantage becomes a fixed reduction in Bob's noise floor, independent of the signal and jamming powers. Within a bounded-collection wiretap model, correlated jamming preserves positive secrecy even when Eve has a stronger direct channel than Bob and remains effective against collective measurements on Eve's Gaussian output states. The protocol supports bright classical message transmission and requires no end-to-end quantum channel. Possible applications include shot-noise-limited optical communication, cryogenic microwave networks, and covert or power-constrained secure links.

fields.title: Volume VI: Residual Risk and Readiness Metrics: Logical Error, Modular Memory, Cryo-CMOS Power and Entanglement Overheads
fields.description: This sixth volume quantifies residual risks that remain after the modular cryogenic, cryo-CMOS, memory and entanglement stack examined in Volumes III–V. Four binding constraints are treated: logical error rates required for chemical accuracy and cryptographic relevance; modular integration of quantum memory cells inside shared cryogenic volumes; power budgets of cryo-CMOS controllers relative to dilution-refrigerator cooling capacity; and the additional overhead imposed by fermionic superselection rules on molecular entanglement measures. Each constraint is mapped onto concrete readiness indicators for molecular simulation and for post-quantum migration. The analysis shows that physical-layer demonstrations (15-second coherence, 99.3 % L-coupler fidelity, cryo-CMOS two-qubit errors ~2.3 × 10^{-3}) do not yet close the logical and integration gaps. Readiness is therefore expressed as a set of measurable thresholds rather than as a single predicted year.

fields.title: Heavy metal ion driven smart nanomaterials for multimodal sensing, biocomputing, and information security: a mini review
fields.description: Heavy metal ions (HMIs) are widely recognized as persistent environmental pollutants. However, they are increasingly being employed as functional chemical inputs in intelligent molecular systems. This mini review summarizes smart nanomaterial-based platforms developed for HMI-driven biocomputing and information security. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of dual-mode, multimode, and multichannel readout strategies that translate selective ion-recognition and signal-transduction events into fluorescence, colorimetric, electrochemical, and other measurable responses. By converting these responses into binary states, such platforms can execute diverse molecular logic operations, parity functions, and arithmetic functions. Their applications in information security, including ASCII- and Morse-code-based encryption, multimodal cryptosteganography, and anti-counterfeiting strategies based on invisible fluorescent inks, are also discussed. Collectively, these studies underscore the potential of HMIs to serve as chemically specific inputs in nanosystems, enhancing sensitive signal transduction and programmable functions for molecular computation and security applications, while reframing toxic pollutants as functional triggers in intelligent chemical platforms.

fields.title: URBAN AIR MOBILITY
fields.description: Scaling Urban Air Mobility (UAM) to thousands of daily operations is limited less by vehicle performance than by the absence of an integrated architecture for airspace management, ground infrastructure and safety assurance. This paper presents a system-of-systems framework for near-ground airspace operated by software rather than human controllers. The framework combines a four-layer onboard autonomy stack with deterministic fallbacks; a three-layer performance-based altitude stratification up to 3,000 ft AGL; 4D space-time trajectory contracts; a low-altitude zero-trust security architecture using post-quantum cryptography; vertiports with battery-buffered megawatt charging; and environmental-resilience measures for urban-canyon microclimates, vortex ring state and wake turbulence. Analytical sizing examples for the wing spar, acoustic barriers and charging buffers are included. All thresholds are design targets obtained by analysis; no flight-test validation is claimed. Open problems, notably the certification of machine-learning components, are identified together with a validation roadmap.

fields.title: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Entanglement Routing in Quantum Networks: Protocols, Repeater Topologies, and Co-Existence with Post-Quantum Cryptography
fields.description: The impending realization of fault-tolerant quantum computers threatens the foundational public-key cryptography underpinning global telecommunications and financial infrastructure. fields.title: Designing an Educational Planning Model Based on the Agricultural Value Chain with a Qualitative Approach
fields.description: Educational planning based on the agricultural value chain, as a comprehensive and systematic approach, can make a substantial contribution to improving quality and productivity in the agricultural sector. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to design an educational planning model based on the agricultural value chain in citrus orchards in northern Iran. This study is classified as qualitative grounded-theory research. The statistical population consisted of 20 experts and faculty members of the Agricultural Research, Education and Extension Organization. Interviews were used for data collection, and MAXQDA 2020 software was employed for data analysis. The findings identified the research components, including causal conditions consisting of core content, educational activities, and supplementary programs; the central phenomenon, namely educational programs based on the agricultural value chain; contextual factors including macro-level policies and culture; intervening factors including evaluation, core policies, competition, and educational approaches; strategies including organizational strategies and environmental strategies; and outcomes including optimal value chain management, quality orientation, and educational enhancement.

fields.title: Open Innovation Adoption Barriers: A Multidimensional Meta-Synthesis and Contextual Prioritization Framework
fields.description: The objective of this study was to systematically identify, synthesize, classify, and prioritize the barriers to open innovation adoption by developing an integrated multidimensional framework that explains the interrelated organizational, behavioral, structural, capability-based, inter-organizational, and institutional obstacles that hinder effective implementation of open innovation across diverse organizational contexts. This study employed a qualitative meta-synthesis design following the seven-step procedure proposed by Sandelowski and Barroso. fields.title: Designing an Employee-Based Brand Equity (Human Resources) Model in the Hotel Industry of Iraq
fields.description: This study was conducted with the aim of identifying and analyzing the dimensions and relationships influencing employee-based brand equity in the Iraqi hotel industry. The research adopted a mixed-methods, sequential design comprising qualitative and quantitative phases. Data analysis was carried out using thematic analysis with MAXQDA software. In the quantitative phase, data obtained from 200 valid questionnaires were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). fields.title: Roadmap for the Prosperity of the Parts Manufacturing Industry in Iran
fields.description: The aim of this research was to develop a roadmap for the prosperity of the parts manufacturing industry in Iran. The present research is qualitative in terms of approach and developmental in terms of objective. The statistical population was in the form of an expert group, including officials and senior managers and experts familiar with the research topic, in the research area. In-depth interviews and group analysis were used to collect research data. The validity and reliability of the findings were examined and confirmed by external reviewers and triangulation. Reliability was also confirmed based on Cohen's Kappa index, with a numerical value of 0.726. In order to analyze the qualitative data, content analysis based on the data obtained from the interviews was used.The conceptual model consisted of 12 main aspects, including 146 indicators or concepts of the evaluator, which were obtained through the integration and classification of the tips or guide codes. The main dimensions in the model include: factors of production boom from the perspective of resources and infrastructure in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 16 structures and 35 evaluators, factors of production boom from the perspective of technology in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 8 structures (2 main and 6 secondary) and 19 evaluators, and factors of production boom from the perspective of trends and directions in product development in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 12 structures and 34 evaluators. The final findings led to the creation of a strategic model in the form of a roadmap for production boom in longitudinal and functional directions that can be used as a comprehensive guide in line with the strategic direction in the said industry

fields.title: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Psychological Flexibility and Suicidal Ideation in Women with Experiences of Spousal Infidelity
fields.description: Objective: The present study aimed to determine the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy on psychological flexibility and suicidal ideation in women with experiences of spousal infidelity. Methods and Materials: The present study employed a quasi-experimental design with a pretest–posttest structure and a control group. The statistical population consisted of women with experiences of spousal infidelity who were referred to the Arsam Psychological and Counseling Services Center in Tonekabon in 2026. Using convenience sampling, 28 participants were selected and randomly assigned into experimental and control groups, with 14 participants in each group. Data collection instruments included the Psychological Flexibility Questionnaire developed by Dennis and Vander Wal and the Suicide Ideation Questionnaire developed by Keith. The experimental group received cognitive behavioral therapy during eight 90-minute sessions, while the control group received no intervention during the study period. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and analysis of covariance in SPSS software. Findings: The findings indicated that cognitive behavioral therapy significantly improved psychological flexibility in women with experiences of spousal infidelity. The results of covariance analysis demonstrated a statistically significant difference between the experimental and control groups in posttest psychological flexibility scores after controlling for pretest scores (F = 53.56, p < .001, η² = .59). In addition, cognitive behavioral therapy significantly reduced suicidal ideation among participants in the experimental group compared with the control group (F = 45.32, p < .001, η² = .56). Conclusion: The findings suggest that cognitive behavioral therapy is an effective psychological intervention for increasing psychological flexibility and reducing suicidal ideation among women affected by spousal infidelity.

fields.description: Introduction: The impact of testosterone therapy on the hormone cycles, exercise capacity, and physiology of transmasculine individuals is not well understood. Existing studies report limited metrics at large time intervals between data collection points. Methods: High-resolution temporal data were collected from a single amateur trans male triathlete over 13 months-including one baseline month and 12 months on testosterone therapy-to characterize hormone, strength, body composition, aerobic, and training load profiles. Results: ) were associated with both training and testosterone levels, with future work needed to untangle their relative contributions. Conclusion: This study provides the most comprehensive characterization of the impacts of testosterone therapy on hormone cycles, exercise capacity, and physiological changes in a single person to date, as well as observations to help inform the design of larger cohort studies.

fields.title: Comparison of the effects of AI-generated music on emotional responses, aesthetic enjoyment, and perceived quality between musicians and non-musicians
fields.description: This study investigates how emotional responses, aesthetic enjoyment, and perceived quality elicited by artificial intelligence (AI)-generated music differ between musicians and non-musicians using a mixed-methods research design. fields.title: Application of medical gases in prevention and treatment of electromagnetic radiation injury.
fields.description: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. NO plays a dual role as both a cytoprotectant and a mediator of bystander effect propagation. Hyperbaric oxygen enhances systemic resilience through preconditioning. Delivery strategies have evolved from conventional inhalation and oral administration toward smart nanocarriers and stimuli-responsive donor systems. However, these platforms still face challenges in spatiotemporal control and long-term safety. Furthermore, broader limitations, including an uneven research distribution across electromagnetic wavebands, a scarcity of clinical trials, and the lack of non-invasive methods for real-time gas concentration monitoring, are comprehensively discussed.

fields.title: Experimental evidence for the beneficial effects of low-concentration ozone.
fields.description: Ozone (O3), a molecule consisting of three oxygen atoms, is an unstable compound whose clinical application as a complementary therapy continues to expand. Although numerous clinical studies support its therapeutic potential, the molecular basis of its effects has remained poorly understood. This review summarizes the current knowledge on the cellular and molecular mechanisms activated by low-concentration O3. Central to its action is the induction of mild oxidative stress by low concentrations of O3, which triggers an antioxidant response mediated through nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2, enhancing cell survival. Additionally, low-concentration O3 exhibits antiinflammatory properties by modulating cytokine expression, inhibiting metalloproteinases, and activating macrophages. The regenerative potential of low-concentration O3 may be attributed to the stimulation of fibroblasts, chondrocytes, and osteoblasts. Moreover, the antitumor effects of low-concentration O3 in cancer cell lines and animal models appear to be linked to the inhibition of cell proliferation and migration, as well as proapoptotic activity. More research is needed to determine the best treatment methods, long-term effectiveness, and standardized clinical procedures for ozone therapy in specific diseases. This review provides a detailed reference for understanding how O3 therapy works.

fields.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
fields.description: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

fields.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
fields.description: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

fields.title: Medical gases and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: therapeutic mechanisms and research advances.
fields.description: Hypertensive disorders during pregnancy pose a serious threat to the health of both mothers and infants, yet the range of available clinical treatments is limited. This review summarizes the mechanisms and recent advances in the use of medical gases, such as nitric oxide, hyperbaric oxygen, carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide, in the treatment of this condition. These gaseous molecules have unique protective effects, including regulating vascular tone, improving placental blood perfusion and inhibiting oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. However, their clinical application faces major challenges, including precise dose control, optimization of delivery methods and assessment of long-term safety. While this review suggests that medical gas therapy provides new avenues for research and potential applications in the management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, it also highlights the need for further basic and clinical studies to clarify their precise mechanisms.

fields.title: Molecular crosstalk between gas transmitters and catecholamine biosynthesis pathways: a narrative review.
fields.description: Catecholamines, particularly the hormone and neurotransmitter epinephrine, are important regulators of blood pressure and cardiovascular function. The expression of genes encoding catecholamine biosynthetic enzymes is subject to strict transcriptional regulation through both hormonal and neuronal mechanisms. These genes are also regulated by hypoxia and reactive oxygen species. A class of small gaseous transmitters, known as gas transmitters, serve as potent regulators of blood pressure and hypoxic signaling; however, their roles in catecholamine biosynthesis remain poorly understood. This manuscript reviews the current state of catecholamine and gas transmitter research, particularly their interactions in relation to hypertension. Current evidence shows that the gas transmitters nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide modulate catecholamine biosynthesis and release through both shared and distinct mechanisms. This regulation is highly dependent on concentration, cellular context, and mode of delivery. Additionally, this review explores hypoxic signaling as a link between catecholamines and gas transmitters. Together, these findings highlight a complex and context-dependent regulatory signaling between gas transmitters and catecholamines. Further mechanistic studies investigating endogenous signaling are required to elucidate these interactions and their therapeutic potential.

This manuscript reviews the current state of catecholamine and gas transmitter research, particularly their interactions in relation to hypertension. Current evidence shows that the gas transmitters nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide modulate catecholamine biosynthesis and release through both shared and distinct mechanisms. This regulation is highly dependent on concentration, cellular context, and mode of delivery. Additionally, this review explores hypoxic signaling as a link between catecholamines and gas transmitters. Together, these findings highlight a complex and context-dependent regulatory signaling between gas transmitters and catecholamines. Further mechanistic studies investigating endogenous signaling are required to elucidate these interactions and their therapeutic potential.

fields.title: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitric oxide: role in the pathophysiology of obstructive sleep apnea.
fields.description: Obstructive sleep apnea is a prevalent sleep-related breathing disorder with recurrent episodes of upper airway collapse during sleep, leading to cyclic blood gas fluctuations. Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitric oxide play a crucial role in the pathophysiology. This narrative review aims to explore the role of gases in obstructive sleep apnea pathophysiology, focusing on the molecular pathways and effects of chronic intermittent hypoxia, intermittent hypercapnia, and nitric oxide dysregulation. Chronic intermittent hypoxia stimulates molecular pathways such as hypoxia-inducible factor-1α and inflammatory cascades such as nuclear factor kappa B, leading to oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and sympathetic overactivation. Intermittent hypercapnia impacts on chemoreflex sensitivity, ventilatory instability, and autonomic function, with emerging evidence of both pathogenic and potentially beneficial effects. Nitric oxide, which modulates airway tone, vascular reactivity, and immune control, presents a reduced bioavailability in patients with obstructive sleep apnea. These three gas mediators contribute to the complex pathophysiology of obstructive sleep apnea and underlie the long-term cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurocognitive risks of obstructive sleep apnea. Appropriately prioritizing the relationship between these gases and the pathophysiology of obstructive sleep apnea contributes to a new understanding of the disease and new treatment approaches in the future.

fields.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
fields.description: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

fields.title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health.
fields.description: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.

fields.title: Ambient particulate matter pollution and stroke burden.
fields.description: As a major component of air pollution, ambient particulate matter pollution has rarely been studied with respect to its global stroke burden. This study aims to evaluate the global stroke incidence, mortality, and health inequalities related to ambient particulate matter pollution from 1990 to 2021. Utilizing the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, we analyzed global stroke-related mortality, disability-adjusted life years, and their age-standardized rates. The estimated annual percentage change was calculated using a linear regression model. Health inequalities were measured using the concentration index and slope index of inequality. China experienced the largest increases in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, Vietnam had the fastest rise in age-standardized mortality rates, the Russian Federation saw the steepest declines in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, and Estonia had the most rapid drop in age-standardized mortality rate. fields.title: Phenotypic Evaluation of Sunflower (Helianthus Annuus L.) Landraces as a Tool for Conservation and Valorization of Plant Genetic Resources
fields.description: Sunflower yield stagnation driven by genetic erosion threatens edible oil security, necessitates the integration of adaptive genetic resources. This study conducted the phenotypic valorization of 114 Pakistan's indigenous sunflower landraces along with 3 checks to characterize genetic diversity, analyze yield-associated traits, and identify superior genotypes for sunflower improvement programs. The experiment was conducted in an augmented block design using six blocks at the Agriculture Research Farm, Hazara University, Mansehra. Data on 9 morpho-yield related traits were analyzed using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), principal component analysis (PCA), cluster analysis, and correlation analysis. Highly significant differences (p<0.001) were observed for treatments, and 'Checks vs. Varieties' highlights considerable genetic variability in the germplasm. Adjusted means performance revealed that Atika-09 (1947.5 kg ha-1), Atika-11 (2427.3 kg ha⁻¹), and Mehraj-10 (1502.4 kg ha-1) showed superior performance across important yield and adaptive traits. PCA revealed that seed yield (PC1) and disease incidence (PC2) accounted for 49.29% of the variation among genotypes. Cluster analysis grouped the genotypes into two clusters, dividing them into 4 groups and 8 subgroups, with group A1 comprising superior lines for yield stability and resistance. Seed yield showed a strong positive correlation with plant height (r = 0.54**), head diameter (r = 0.36**), and harvest index (r = 0.92**). The results demonstrate that phenotypic selection, supported by multivariate analysis, can effectively accelerate the development of resilient high-yielding sunflower hybrids for Pakistan’s cropping systems. These findings provide a valuable genetic foundation for breeding programs targeting resilience and yield stability in sunflowers.

fields.title: To Transmit or Not: Tiny On-Device Transformers for Uplink Prediction in Direct-to-Satellite IoT
fields.description: Direct-to-Satellite IoT (DtS-IoT) promises to connect massive fleets of devices in regions where terrestrial infrastructure will never reach. Its weakest link, however, is the device itself: DtS-IoT nodes are inexpensive, energy-constrained, and effectively blind, since downlink feedback from sporadically passing Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites is broadcast, slow, and costly, so in practice devices cannot expect their transmissions to be acknowledged. The satellite cannot micromanage its fleet: every transmission decision must be made on-device, based solely on local information, and every wasted uplink drains energy and fuels collisions. We argue that these decisions can be learned, provided the models are small enough to run on highly constrained hardware and to be updated over a scarce downlink. This paper presents a tiny encoder-only Transformer (14k parameters, 64 KB) that predicts, from the device's recent transmission context, whether an uplink will be received. To address the scarcity of DtS-IoT data, we generate synthetic datasets using the open-source FLORASAT simulator and introduce an ML Sandbox module that embeds trained models directly into the simulation for closed-loop evaluation. Deployed in that closed loop, the model delivers 16.1% more unique packets than an unguided baseline while sending 41.6% fewer transmissions, and its operating frontier dominates a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) of comparable footprint, an analytical linkbudget policy, and the blind repetition budget itself: spending the same energy without the model delivers 2.3× fewer packets. Both gains are the currency that matters for blind, battery-powered devices: more data through, less energy spent.

fields.title: Deep Learning-based Method for Removing Inter-layer Aliasing Artifacts in Computed Laminography Reconstruction
fields.description: Computed laminography (CL) — featuring a tilted scanning configuration—mitigates the constraints of computerized tomography on X-ray energy and scanning space when inspecting plate-like objects. However, this design compromises the completeness of projection data, thus causing interlayer aliasing artifacts in reconstructed images. Hence, this study proposes an image post-processing approach. Specifically, a U-shaped neural network model integrating Swin Transformer blocks and attention mechanisms is developed to refine low-quality images corrupted by aliasing artifacts. An anisotropic composite loss function is derived to enhance the restoration of edge details in images. Finally, a feature-fusion technique is employed to correct the network’s output. Experiments conducted on simulated printed circuit board datasets demonstrate that the proposed method improves the peak signal noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of SART-reconstructed results by 144.73% and 68.10%, respectively. It effectively eliminates aliasing artifacts and recovers the correct structural information of objects.

fields.title: Gecombineerde en gepersonaliseerde oncolytische virotherapie in de strijd tegen glioblastoma
fields.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive type of primary brain tumor in adults and remains associated with a poor prognosis despite standard-of-care treatment consisting of surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. The highly heterogeneous nature of GBM contributes to frequent therapeutic resistance and tumor recurrence, highlighting the urgent need for novel treatment strategies. These findings indicate that diverse OVs share similar determinants of oncolytic activity and suggest that tumor subtype may guide the selection of the optimal OV. Finally, subpopulations of GBM-PDCLs resistant to OVs were selected and compared to their parental GBM-PDCL to identify resistance mechanisms. Downregulation of glutamate receptor signaling was identified as a shared resistance mechanism, while collagen fibril organization was specifically downregulated in Sindbis-resistant GBM-PDCLs but upregulated in H1-parvovirus-resistant GBM-PDCLs. In addition, resistance to multiple OVs was associated with upregulation of antiviral immune responses, with a dependency on chronic type I interferon signaling for survival. These observations show that resistance is driven by both shared and virus-specific cellular processes, underscoring the complexity of OV response and resistance in GBM. This work demonstrates that susceptibility to OVs in GBM can be influenced by (a combination of) virus-specific host factors, tumor subtypes and intrinsic cellular processes such as antiviral defense, neurodevelopmental and ECM-related mechanisms. These findings support the development of biomarker-driven patient stratification, rational OV combinations and adaptive treatment strategies, paving the way towards more personalized and effective oncolytic virotherapy approaches in GBM.

fields.title: Pectinase-Based Bioprocesses for Circular Bioeconomy and Sustainable Industrial Development.
fields.description: Pectinases play a vital role in the degradation of pectic part of the plant cell wall and are considered in the group of hydrolytic enzymes. In the present scenario, demand of economically feasible and environment friendly techniques and approaches has significantly led the research on the microbial production, standardization of process parameters and improvements of pectinases. The development of pectinase-based bioprocesses has been found to promote sustainable industrial practices by reducing the use of chemicals, energy, and waste, thereby supporting eco-friendly production systems. The unique aspect of this review is that it explains traditional methods of pectinase production alongside novel methods, which include solid-state and submerged fermentation, recombinant DNA techniques, heterologous gene expression, protein engineering, CRISPR/Cas genome editing technologies, enzyme immobilization, and nanobiotechnological methods, which improve the production, stability, and performance of pectinases. It further demonstrates the increasing importance of the use of pectinases in sustainable manufacturing through decreasing the use of chemicals and energy, as well as reducing waste production from industry. It illustrates that innovations in microbial strain engineering, process optimization, and utilization of low-cost substrates have significantly increased the economic viability and efficiency of producing pectinases. Yet, some issues associated with commercialization, standardization of production processes, recovery, and stability of enzymes still exist. Overall, this review paper gives an overview of the recent advancements and limitations of next-generation pectinases.

fields.title: Discovery of Potent and Non-cytotoxic HDAC3-Selective Degraders Featuring a Propyl Hydrazide Zinc-Binding Group
fields.description: Abstract Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an important therapeutic target in cancer, yet selective HDAC3 degraders remain limited. In this study, we report the development of novel class I HDAC degraders derived from the HDAC3-preferential inhibitor FL-007. Two linker exit vectors were investigated, leading to the identification of a series of potent compounds (2a−d) exhibiting low micromolar inhibition of HDAC2 and submicromolar inhibition of HDAC1 and HDAC3, together with selective HDAC3 degradation. Degradation activity was confirmed in MM.1S, HCT116, A2780-HDAC3-HiBiT, and Cal27CisR cells using immunoblotting and HiBiT/LgBiT assays, achieving Dmax values of up to 92%. Notably, these compounds showed no cytotoxicity up to 100 μM in both cancerous and non-cancerous cell lines. Selective HDAC3 degradation resulted in moderate chemosensitization of cisplatin-resistant Cal27CisR cells, in contrast to the stronger effects observed with cytotoxic HDAC inhibitors. For compound 2b, the chemosensitizing effect was associated with increased histone H3 acetylation and increased p21 expression.
