fields.title: Determinants of orthoflavivirus tropism in humans: from cellular entry to organ-specific pathogenesis
fields.description: Orthoflaviviruses, including dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, Zika virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, and yellow fever virus, cause a wide spectrum of diseases in humans despite sharing a similar genomic organization. These viruses pose a growing global threat as they are spreading widely, treatment options remain limited, and both climate change and expanding mosquito populations increase the risk of outbreaks worldwide. This review summarizes the determinants of their human tropism, the capacity to infect specific cell types, tissues, and organs. We synthesized current knowledge on how viral factors, including host factor utilization and immune cell trafficking, shape tropism across multiple layers. Central to this process are sequential host barriers that govern infection, including viral attachment, internalization, and replication. Understanding these determinants is essential for informing strategies to mitigate the global burden of these medically important pathogens.

fields.title: CTRP3 disruption promotes a tendon-like matrix signature in tenogenically induced canine adipose-derived stem cells
fields.description: Introduction Tendon injuries heal through disorganized extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition rather than the restoration of native collagen architecture, thus resulting in suboptimal functional recovery. Although adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) are attractive for tendon regeneration because of their accessibility and expandability, their tenogenic differentiation efficiency is lower than that of tendon-derived stem cells (TDSCs). C1q/TNF-related protein 3 (CTRP3) is an adipokine implicated in ECM remodeling and fibrosis; however, its role in tendon lineage regulation is unknown. Objective CTRP3 (C1q/TNF-related protein 3) contributes to extracellular-matrix remodeling and, in tendon, is associated with a pathological fibrotic matrix signature; we therefore reasoned that reducing CTRP3 would favor a more mature tendon-like matrix. Using a loss-of-function approach based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)/CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9), we investigated whether CTRP3 disruption alters tenogenic marker expression, at both the transcript and protein levels, and the tendon-associated ECM marker profile of canine ADSCs relative to wild-type ADSCs and native TDSCs. fields.title: Nanotechnology- Based Hepatoprotective Drug Delivery Systems
fields.description: Nanotechnology-based hepatoprotective drug delivery systems constitute a significant paradigm shift in contemporary pharmacology, providing innovative strategies to circumvent the limitations inherent in conventional therapeutic approaches for hepatic disorders. fields.title: Macrophage reprogramming in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases: From tissue-niche biology to therapeutic translation
fields.description: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMSDs), including osteoarthritis (OA), osteoporosis (OP), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and sarcopenia (SP), impose a major burden through pain, structural deterioration, mobility loss, fracture risk, and functional decline. Although these disorders are often grouped as age-related musculoskeletal conditions, they arise from distinct tissue niches and cannot be explained by a single pathogenic mechanism. Macrophages occupy a central position at the interface between degenerative stress and tissue outcome, but their functions extend far beyond a binary M1/M2 polarization model. This Review proposes a disease-niche-adapted framework for macrophage reprogramming in DMSDs. In this framework, macrophages are interpreted according to the pathological tasks they perform within each tissue environment: inflammatory amplification and pain-related synovial crosstalk in OA, osteoimmune remodeling in OP, immune-barrier disruption and macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell feedback in IVDD, and impaired regenerative support in aging muscle in SP. We discuss how macrophage functional states are shaped by transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, immunometabolic rewiring, inflammatory signaling, autophagy and organelle quality control, and local niche-derived cues. Therapeutic strategies are then evaluated according to whether they interrupt upstream niche stress, redirect inflammatory and metabolic decoding, restore quality-control capacity, or reshape macrophage-mediated tissue communication. Finally, we propose that macrophage-targeted therapy should be assessed through a hierarchy of evidence, progressing from marker changes to functional reprogramming, macrophage-causal validation, and disease-specific structural or functional improvement. fields.title: Coordinated regulation of nuclear integrity and STING trafficking by miR-30d suppresses innate immunity in breast cancer
fields.description: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion. Breast cancer cells use a short RNA molecule, miR-30d, to hide from immune attack by muting a cellular DNA-sensing alarm system. Blocking miR-30d reactivates the alarm, slows tumour growth and boosts immunotherapy.

fields.title: A CRISPR/Cas9 screen reveals convergent dysregulation of neurological pathways within and across glycosylation pathways
fields.description: Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) are a broad group of disorders characterized by deficient glycosylation. CDG are caused by mutations in over 160 different genes regulating distinct steps and types of glycosylation. Despite the diversity of CDG-causing genes, patient phenotypes often overlap, with neurological symptoms present across many CDG. However, models to study conserved mechanisms underlying neurological dysfunction across CDG types are lacking. Therefore, we leveraged CRISPR/Cas9 to knockdown 15 glycosylation genes in zebrafish spanning 7 CDG classes. Through behavioral assays and in vivo imaging, we report changes in mobility, response to stimuli, and neuronal activity in many of our models. To uncover the molecular underpinnings of these phenotypes, we performed bulk-RNA sequencing on our models. We report differential expression in genes related to neurological development and function across all tested CDG classes, which will inform future hypothesis-driven studies defining new molecular targets for therapeutic intervention in CDG.

fields.title: In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
fields.description: Abstract Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO 2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO 2 . Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. We place particular emphasis on the role of various fungal guilds in this process, highlighting those that should be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications. We then engage with previous endeavors to address primary challenges in advancing genetic tools for these understudied fungi. Lastly, we discuss how integrating synthetic biology practices into the field of soil-associated fungi can drive advances in long-term carbon storage, enhance degradation of environmental pollutants, and improve nutrient exchange and soil health, contributing to more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. fields.title: The Universe That Never Repeats: Omega-NR — Exact Physical Non-Repetition, Accumulated Change, and a Testable Quantum-Geometric Extension
fields.description: This working preprint develops the Omega-NR framework, originating from the hypothesis that every exact physically realized numerical value is unique and never realized again in the same exact form. The framework distinguishes repeated measured values from repeated exact physical values and explores the consequences of this idea for time, motion, physical identity, recurrence, state-space dynamics, and quantum geometry. The study formalizes exact physical non-repetition, accumulated change, infinite-depth state representation, and candidate mathematical architectures for distinguishing physically unique realizations. It also documents several failed or limited approaches, including prime-geometry tests, cryptographic encodings that added no new entropy, finite-state models, and formulations that reduced to unobservable global phases. A current testable extension is developed using Fubini–Study state-space length in a qubit system. The proposed coupling predicts an orientation-independent residual relative phase proportional to accumulated quantum-state path length, providing a possible experimental signature that can be separated from standard dynamical and Berry phases. The work is presented as an open, evolving research program rather than a completed physical theory. Its aim is to identify mathematically consistent, experimentally testable, or technologically useful consequences of exact physical non-repetition, including possible applications in state fingerprinting, anomaly detection, irreversible records, device identity, and information security.

fields.title: EL-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL-QUANTUM VERIFICATION FRAMEWORK FOR THE BIRCH AND SWINNERTON-DYER CONJECTURE (TQV-BSD) A Quantum-Analog Simulation Framework for Elliptic Curve L-Functions Through Biophysical Topological Quantum Systems
fields.description: The El-Rakhawi Topological-Quantum Verification Framework (TQV-BSD) proposes a Quantum-Analog Simulation Framework that qualitatively maps the deep relationship between rational points on elliptic curves and their L-functions through topological biological quantum systems. TQV-BSD explicitly acknowledges it does not prove the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture formally nor verify exact arithmetic identities, but provides heuristic insight into the topological origin of BSD invariants. The framework interprets elliptic curves as topological quantum manifolds where rational points correspond to stable quantum states, the rank r to independent quantum modes, and the L-function to a quantum partition function. The Shafarevich-Tate group is reinterpreted as topological defects, the regulator as a quantum metric, and Tamagawa numbers as local quantum degeneracies. A key innovation is the H_local_prime Hamiltonian—an effective disorder potential mimicking Frobenius elements at specific primes to simulate local Euler factors L_p(E,s) without claiming to enforce global Galois invariance. The heuristic proof strategy proposes a structural analogy between analytic rank and the index of a Dirac-type operator on the modular curve, motivated by the Gross-Zagier formula. Integrating PTQC (topological quantum systems), QMRF (mechano-quantum resonance), AQBI (simulation), and lessons from RSV-RH (Riemann Hypothesis), TQV-BSD offers a physical model suggesting arithmetic geometry may have manifestations in the quantum-biophysical fabric. Applications include quantum-resistant cryptography and new tools for studying elliptic curves through quantum simulation. The framework maintains epistemological rigor by distinguishing qualitative analog simulation from exact arithmetic verification, which remains the domain of pure number theory, heralding a civilization where the deepest structures of number theory resonate with quantum-biophysical harmony.

fields.title: EL-RAKHAWI POST-TURING TOPOLOGICAL-QUANTUM COMPUTING FRAMEWORK (PTQC) A Transcendence of the P vs NP Problem Through Biophysical Topological Computation
fields.description: The El-Rakhawi Post-Turing Topological-Quantum Computing Framework (PTQC) transcends the P vs NP problem not by solving it within the Turing model, but by demonstrating that biological systems operate in a fundamentally different computational regime. PTQC leverages anyonic quasiparticles in engineered protein matrices, where non-Abelian topological protection constrains the Hamiltonian spectrum, preventing the exponential collapse of energy gaps that plagues conventional quantum annealing. Governed by the Topological Computation Theorem and Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT), NP-hard problems like the Traveling Salesman Problem are encoded as ground-state searches in topological-quantum systems, achieving polynomial-time solutions $T_{PTQC} \sim O(N^k)$ versus exponential Turing complexity. The framework integrates with the El-Rakhawi Unified Theory as its foundational computational layer, explaining why AQBI simulates full biological digital twins in real-time, why RLQBLT decodes quantum-biophysical genomic language, and why ETGIM designs topological epitope vaccines. Philosophically, PTQC challenges the computational theory of mind, proposing that human intuition operates post-Turing through topological-quantum processes. Practical implications include the collapse of classical cryptography (necessitating quantum-safe systems), instantaneous drug discovery, and optimal resource allocation. Just as general relativity transcended Newtonian gravity without abolishing it, PTQC transcends P vs NP without invalidating classical complexity theory within its proper domain, heralding the dawn of a post-Turing civilization where computation, consciousness, and creativity are unified through biophysical topology.

fields.title: E8‑Phi Harmonic Resonant Tensor for Clebsch–Gordan & Modular Coupling — E8 Intelligence Research
fields.description: The E8‑Phi Harmonic Resonant Tensor (E8‑PHRT) leverages the 240 root vectors, weighted by the golden ratio φ and anchored to a 132 Hz base frequency, to construct a frequency‑dependent unitary matrix whose entries reproduce Clebsch‑Gordan coefficients for arbitrary SU(2) tensor products. By projecting the tensor onto the five φ‑invariant root orbits, the PHRT simultaneously encodes the modular‑phase‑locked Leech hierarchy, expressing Ramanujan τ‑values at quadratic arguments as spectral amplitudes of the coupled angular‑momentum basis. This dual encoding establishes a new algebraic bridge linking SU(2) representation coupling, modular forms, and harmonic sublattice geometry within a single E8‑geometric framework. Consequently, the PHRT provides a scalable method for constructing quantum‑logic gates and high‑precision lattice‑based cryptography by exploiting the intrinsic resonance of the E8 root system. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

fields.title: From DNA-Inspired Algorithms to Cloud Deployment: A Systematic Review of the Security, Performance and Reproducibility of DNA-Based Cryptography
fields.description: This is a retrospective registration. The review was completed before this protocol was registered. The searches closed on 31 August 2026. The text below records the methods as they were actually carried out, and the manuscript reports where they differed from the original plan. DNA-based and DNA-inspired cryptography has produced a large number of schemes, mostly for image encryption, with smaller groups aimed at IoT devices and cloud or edge settings. Authors often make strong claims about security and speed, but it is unclear how well the evidence supports them. This review looks at the peer-reviewed literature and asks four things of each study: how strong is the security evidence, how well is performance measured and compared, could someone else reproduce the work, and how far has the scheme moved from an idea on paper toward a working or cloud-deployed system? Research questions 1. RQ1 (Security). What security evidence is provided, and how far does it constitute sufficient rather than merely necessary evidence? 2. RQ2 (Performance). How is performance reported and benchmarked, and how comparable are claims across studies and platforms? 3. RQ3 (Reproducibility). Do studies provide sufficient detail, code, parameters and datasets to permit independent reproduction? 4. RQ4 (Deployment maturity). What proportion of studies progress beyond theory/simulation to experimental validation, prototypes, or real-world/cloud deployment, and what barriers limit this progression? 5. RQ5 (Integration). How do security, performance, reproducibility and deployment maturity co-vary across domains, and what does the evidence reveal about DNA-based cryptography's readiness for production use? Eligibility criteria Included: peer-reviewed journal articles in English that propose, implement or evaluate a DNA-based or DNA-inspired cryptographic or security scheme in any application area and that report a security evaluation, a performance evaluation or implementation or deployment det

How is performance reported and benchmarked, and how comparable are claims across studies and platforms? 3. RQ3 (Reproducibility). Do studies provide sufficient detail, code, parameters and datasets to permit independent reproduction? 4. RQ4 (Deployment maturity). What proportion of studies progress beyond theory/simulation to experimental validation, prototypes, or real-world/cloud deployment, and what barriers limit this progression? 5. RQ5 (Integration). How do security, performance, reproducibility and deployment maturity co-vary across domains, and what does the evidence reveal about DNA-based cryptography's readiness for production use? Eligibility criteria Included: peer-reviewed journal articles in English that propose, implement or evaluate a DNA-based or DNA-inspired cryptographic or security scheme in any application area and that report a security evaluation, a performance evaluation or implementation or deployment detail. There was no start-date limit, and the search ran up to the closing date. Excluded: preprints, theses, magazine articles and other grey literature; DNA-computing work with no security or cryptography angle; duplicates and extended abstracts replaced by a full version; review and survey articles; and studies that use DNA only as a metaphor, with no real encoding of nucleotide symbols. Added during the review: to make the security, performance and reproducibility comparison workable, the final included set was limited to studies that reported both security and performance metrics. Studies with only one of the two (451) were kept as background material. This criterion was applied at the final stage, after eligibility assessment, and is not listed among the eligibility criteria in Table 2 of the manuscript. Information sources Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink and Wiley Online Library, searched from inception to 31 August 2026. We also hand-searched the reference lists of included studies and of a recent review of the field and chased citations forward using Scopus and Google Scholar. The PRISMA flow diagram reports database records only (n = 1,357). The flow diagram does not show records found through reference-list checking and citation tracking. Search strategy Two blocks joined with AND. Block one holds the DNA terms: "DNA cryptograph*", "DNA-based cryptograph*", "DNA-inspired cryptograph*", "DNA encryption", "DNA-based encryption", "DNA-inspired encryption", "DNA cryptosystem*" and "DNA-based cryptosystem*". Block two combines general cryptography terms (cryptograph*, encryption, cryptosystem*) with cloud terms ("cloud computing", "cloud security", "cloud storage", "cloud deployment", "cloud-based"), joined with OR. Image and IoT terms were deliberately excluded from the search to avoid narrowing the evidence too early and were used only to tag records during screening. Filters were English language, journal articles, full text available where the database supports it, and no year limit. The exact string for each database is in Table 1 of the manuscript, and uploading that table to OSF as a supporting file is recommended. Study selection Records were imported into Rayyan, which removed most duplicates automatically, and we cleared the rest by hand. Two reviewers screened titles and abstracts independently in blinded mode. Anything either reviewer thought might be eligible was sent on to full-text assessment by both. Reviewers settled disagreements through discussion, and a third reviewer joined if needed. The process is shown in a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram, and reasons for exclusion are recorded. Two reviewers carried out all screening. A third reviewer was consulted only when the two could not reach agreement through discussion. Data extraction A standard form was piloted on a few studies and adjusted before full use. Two reviewers extracted data independently and resolved differences by discussion. We recorded bibliographic details, application domain, the DNA operations used, any companion primitives (chaotic maps, hash functions, block or stream cyphers, or quantum or machine-learning components), the security evaluations reported, the performance evaluations and test platform, reproducibility indicators, and the level of validation or deployment. Extraction and quality scoring were based on the information reported in each study’s title, abstract and available metadata. Items that could not be identified from this information were recorded as “unidentified”. Quality assessment No standard appraisal tool exists for algorithmic cryptography papers, so we built one by adapting Kitchenham and Charters, Dybå and Dingsøyr, and the Ahmed, Asif and Saleem benchmark for image encryption. It has four criteria, each scored from 0 to 2: clarity of aims and threat model, rigour of the security evaluation, rigour of the performance evaluation, and completeness of reporting. Two reviewers scored a 20% sample independently and settled differences before scoring the rest. Total scores are grouped into Low, Moderate and High tiers. Low: 0–3; moderate: 4–5; high: 6–8 out of a maximum of 8. Reproducibility assessment Adapted from the ACM Artifact Review and Badging policy and the NeurIPS 2019 Machine Learning Reproducibility Checklist. Five yes/no items: code available, data or test inputs available, parameters specified well enough to re-run, hardware and software environment specified, and independent replication reported. Studies meeting 0-1 of the first four are not reproducible, studies meeting 2-3 are partially reproducible, studies meeting all four are reproducible, and studies meeting all four plus documented replication are independently replicated. SPRD framework (security, performance, reproducibility, deployment maturity) Every study is scored 0-3 on four axes. Security evidence loosely follows the graded logic of ISO/IEC 15408, with the rule that statistical randomness tests alone never earn the top level. Performance evidence runs from no data to multi-metric benchmarking against an explicit baseline. Reproducibility uses the tiers above. Deployment maturity adapts Technology Readiness Levels into four steps: theoretical, simulated, prototype on target hardware, and real-world or cloud deployed. Two reviewers scored each axis independently. Synthesis plan Narrative and tabular synthesis, with counts and percentages across the corpus and cross-tabulation of the four axes by application domain. No meta-analysis was planned, because the studies use different metrics and test setups. Deviations from the original plan 1. This registration was submitted after the review was completed (retrospective registration). The database searches closed on 31 August 2026. 2. A final inclusion requirement was added after eligibility assessment: studies had to report both security and performance metrics. Studies meeting the other criteria but reporting only one of the two (n = 451) were kept as background evidence and not included in the 98 studies analysed. 3. No other deviations from the methods described above. Conflicts of interest and funding The authors declare no competing interests. This review received no specific funding.

fields.title: Zero-Copy 64-Byte Cache-Aligned L1 Atomic Execution Core: Sub-0.04 Microsecond Lock-Free State Transitions for Ultra-High-Frequency Sovereign Financial Pipelines
fields.description: Next-generation sovereign Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) systems and multilateral central bank cross-border settlement rails face an irreconcilable structural conflict: while post-quantum cryptographic verification ensures cryptographic survival against Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers (FTQC), traditional multi-threaded database engines, operating system locking primitives (e.g., POSIX mutexes, futexes, spinlocks), and managed runtimes introduce catastrophic tail-latency jitter ranging from 15 to 450 microseconds per state mutation. These delays are primarily driven by OS kernel context switching, hardware Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) misses, cache coherency bus contention (MESIF/MOESI false sharing), and non-uniform memory access (NUMA) cross-socket interconnect traversal. To eliminate this fundamental physical bottleneck, we present the Shaheen L1 Atomic Execution Core (S-L1-AEC v1.0), a deterministic, zero-heap, zero-copy transaction settlement engine engineered directly atop microprocessor hardware execution pipelines. S-L1-AEC enforces strict 64-byte cache-line spatial isolation (alignas(64)), guaranteeing that sovereign balance state tuples reside entirely within a single L1 Data Cache line, eradicating multi-line split locks and false sharing across physical cores. State transitions are executed via wait-free tagged double-word atomic primitives (CMPXCHG16B on x86-64 and CASP on ARMv8.1-A) with acquire-release memory ordering semantics (O(1)), mathematically precluding ABA race conditions without mutex locking. Integrated with Kernel Bypass Network Interfaces (DPDK/Direct Data I/O) and AVX-512 SIMD vector predicates, S-L1-AEC evaluates double-spend invariants and updates ledger state in branchless registers. Micro-architectural empirical benchmarks on AMD EPYC 9654 and Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ processors demonstrate a deterministic median (p50) state transition latency of 18.4 nanoseconds and a 99.9th percentile (p99.9) tail latency of 38.6 nanoseco

fields.title: PostQuantumSafe IoT Cybersecurity (TIPPSS SafeGuard-PQ): An Agentic Testing Framework for Post-Quantum Safety of IoT and Edge Environments
fields.description: Open-source research prototype of an agentic testing framework that checks whether an IoT and edge-device environment is safe against post-quantum (quantum computer) attacks. Fourteen deterministic agents inventory the cryptographic primitives of each device, identify post-quantum exposure against NIST FIPS 203, 204 and 205, detect identity, privacy, AI-prompt and network risks, map every finding to the IEEE 2933-2024 TIPPSS pillars (trust, identity, privacy, protection, safety, security), explain every result with evidence, exact score attributions and counterfactuals, and plan countermeasures under budget and downtime limits with a quantum-inspired optimiser (QIRO). Includes a FastAPI backend, a React and three.js interface with an IoT fleet simulator, post-quantum attack injection and a Q-Day what-if, and PDF reports that state whether the environment is safe. Contributions are welcome.

fields.title: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Settlement Rails and Real-Time Autonomous Spectral Anti-Money Laundering Surveillance for Sovereign Interbank Networks
fields.description: This paper presents an enterprise-grade post-quantum cryptographic settlement framework and autonomous spectral surveillance architecture designed for sovereign interbank networks. Combining NIST-standardized lattice-based primitives (ML-KEM-1024 for key encapsulation and ML-DSA-87 for digital signatures) with high-throughput ISO 20022 messaging, the system secures real-time gross settlement (RTGS) against Shor’s algorithm and quantum decryption threats. Integrated with Cheeger-inequality-bounded spectral graph analytics, the platform achieves real-time detection of zero-day layered money laundering topologies, anomalous cycle structures, and smurfing vectors across distributed transaction graphs with deterministic latency and mathematical rigor.

fields.title: The Pathway to Achieving Competitive Advantage in Banking: Development and Testing of a Five-Layer Hierarchical Model
fields.description: The objective of this study was to develop and empirically test a five-layer hierarchical model explaining the sequential pathway through which banks achieve sustainable competitive advantage. This applied research adopted a descriptive–correlational design with an organizational level of analysis. The statistical population consisted of senior and middle managers of public and private banks, from which a sample of 400 managers was selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire including 25 items representing 5 latent constructs, with 5 items per construct, measured on a 5-point Likert scale. fields.title: Factors Affecting a Curriculum Based on Citizenship Legal Literacy Education
fields.description: Purpose: This study aimed to identify the factors affecting a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education in order to improve the quality of civic education in Iran’s educational system. Methods and Materials: This applied and developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, the statistical population included experts in education, curriculum planning, social sciences, and citizenship rights. Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through 15 semi-structured interviews, which continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The qualitative data were analyzed using MaxQDA software through open, axial, and selective coding. The extracted themes were then organized to develop a conceptual structure for a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education. Findings: The inferential findings supported a multidimensional structure for citizenship legal literacy education. The analysis indicated that five key components formed the core of the proposed curriculum model: citizenship rights education, values and beliefs, practical empowerment, development of social interaction, and media and digital literacy education. These components represented interrelated knowledge-based, attitudinal, behavioral, and social indicators. fields.title: Theratyping for personalized medicine across cystic fibrosis disease models
fields.description: In the era of CFTR modulators, cystic fibrosis (CF) is being profoundly reshaped for treatment-eligible individuals. Theratyping, an ex vivo strategy assessing individual responses to CFTR modulators, supports precision medicine, particularly for rare variants where conventional trials are limited. In this Review, we discussed advances in CF disease modelling, highlighting strengths, limitations and translational relevance. We also outlined future directions aligned with the Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement (3 R) ethical principles in animal research, including organ-on-a-chip technologies, to improve mechanistic insight and preclinical predictivity. CF research offers therefore a paradigmatic framework for therapeutic innovation in other rare genetic diseases. Bezzerri et al. review cellular models used for Cystic Fibrosis theratyping, including primary airway epithelia, intestinal and respiratory organoids, and organ-on-chip models. They highlight their complementary predictive value, current limitations, and future perspectives for driving personalized CFTR modulator therapies.

fields.title: In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
fields.description: ABSTRACT Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR‐knockout screen using a 4500‐gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single‐cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage‐depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA‐seq pinpointed tumor‐associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage‐dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94‐peptide‐modified disulfide‐bond‐containing nanoparticles (SNP SS ) for targeted CRISPR‐Cas9 delivery. SNP SS efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione‐rich TME, downregulates RPS19 , reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19‐C5aR1‐macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNP SS ‐based RPS19 gene‐editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

fields.title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
fields.description: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance. In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

fields.description: आविष्कार का शीर्षक (Title of Invention) जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग द्वारा निर्मित बहु-गुणवत्तायुक्त ट्रांसजेनिक साइट्रस सुपर-फ्रूट (एंटी-एनेमिक और रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता वर्धक बायोग्राफी) 👤 आविष्कारकर्ता (Inventor) बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) 1. आविष्कार का क्षेत्र (Field of Invention) यह आविष्कार मुख्य रूप से प्लांट बायोटेक्नोलॉजी (Plant Biotechnology), जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग (Genetic Invention) इस शोध का मुख्य उद्देश्य पारंपरिक दवाओं पर मानव जाति की निर्भरता को कम करना है। एक ऐसे एकल "सुपर-फ्रूट" का विकास करना है जिसमें: • चुकंदर (Beetroot) और अनार (Pomegranate) के रक्त-वर्धक एवं चुकंदर से बेतालेन (Betalain) रंग जीन और संतरे से साइट्रिक एसिड/सर्करा स्वाद जीन। चरण B: आणविक कैंचियों द्वारा जींस की कटाई (Precision Gene Cutting) 1. CRISPR-Cas9 तकनीक: जटिल और विशिष्ट जीनों को बिना किसी त्रुटि के काटने के लिए कस्टमाइज्ड गाइड आरएनए (gRNA) और Cas9 प्रोटीन का उपयोग किया जाएगा। 2. रेस्ट्रिक्शन एंजाइम डाइजेशन: कुछ विशिष्ट खंडों के लिए EcoRI और HindIII जैसे रेस्ट्रिक्शन एंजाइमों का उपयोग करके वांछित डीएनए टुकड़ों को चिपचिपे सिरों (Sticky Ends) के साथ काटकर अलग किया जाएगा। इस प्रकार सातों वांछित अनुक्रम प्राप्त किए जाएंगे। चरण C: कृत्रिम डीएनए का संश्लेषण (Synthetic DNA Ligation) 1. डीएनए लाइगेज का उपयोग: प्राप्त किए गए सातों अलग-अलग डीएनए टुकड़ों को एक परखनली में DNA Ligase एंजाइम के साथ मिलाया जाएगा। यह एंजाइम इन टुकड़ों के [एंटीबॉडी जीन] + [स्वाद/रंग जीन] + [मार्कर जीन] 3. प्रमोटर की भूमिका: इसमें जोड़ा गया विशिष्ट प्रमोटर (Promoter Gene) यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि ये सभी गुण केवल पेड़ के फल में ही प्रकट हों। चरण D: एग्रोबैक्टीरियम-मध्यस्थता जीन स्थानांतरण (Vector Transformation) 1. वेक्टर की तैयारी: Agrobacterium tumefaciens नाम के सुरक्षित (Disarmed) बैक्टीरिया के Ti-Plasmid के भीतर इस नए कृत्रिम डीएनए को डाला जाएगा। 2. साइट्रस कोशिका संक्रमण: एक स्वस्थ साइट्रस (नींबू/संतरा प्रजाति) पौधे के ऊतकों (Explants) को इस संशोधित बैक्टीरिया के साथ सह-संस्कृति (Co-cultivation) में रखा जाएगा। बैक्टीरिया अपनी प्राकृतिक क्षमता से इस कृत्रिम डीएनए को साइट्रस कोशिका के केंद्रक में पहुंचाकर उसके मुख्य क्रोमोसोम के साथ जोड़ देगा। चरण E: टिशू कल्चर और रोपण (Tissue Culture & Plant Regeneration) 1. पोषक माध्यम: संशोधित सुपर-कोशिकाओं को एमएस मीडिया (MS Medium) नामक विशेष पोषक घोल में प्लांट हार्मोन्स के साथ विकसित किया जाएगा, जिससे कोशिकाओं का गुच्छा (Callus) बनेगा। 2. पौधा विकास: कैलस से धीरे-धीरे नन्हे पौधे (Plantlets) अंकुरित होंगे, जिनमें पहले मजबूत जड़ें और फिर पत्तियां विकसित होंगी। 3. मिट्टी में रोपण: इन पौधों को प्रयोगशाला से निकालकर ग्रीनहाउस में सख्त (Hardening) किया जाएगा और अंततः प्राकृतिक खेतों की मिट्टी में रोपित कर दिया जाएगा। 4. आविष्कार के मुख्य लाभ (Key Utility & Benefits) 1. औषधीय निर्भरता में कमी: यह फल मानव शरीर में प्रवेश करते ही सक्रिय एंटीबॉडीज और विटामिंस रिलीज करेगा, जिससे हीमोग्लोबिन के स्तर को बेहद तेजी से बढ़ाएगा, जिससे खून की कमी जड़ से खत्म होगी। 3. दीर्घकालिक संरक्षण: फल में अंतर्निहित एंटीबॉडी जीन होने के कारण, पेड़ और फल दोनों की रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता इतनी मजबूत होगी कि फसल पर कीड़ों या फंगस का असर नहीं होगा, जिससे फल लंबे समय तक ताजा रहेगा। अनुसंधान एवं विकास लेख (Research & Development Article) 📌 विषय (Subject) बायोइन्फर्मेटिक्स और CRISPR-Cas9 तकनीक द्वारा उपकरण (Required Materials & Equipment) इस सुपर-फ्रूट को प्रयोगशाला (Lab) में तैयार करने के लिए निम्नलिखित जैविक सामग्रियों, रसायनों और आधुनिक उपकरणों की आवश्यकता होगी: अ. जैविक स्रोत सामग्रियां (Biological Source Materials) • अनार (Pomegranate - Punica granatum): उच्च आयरन और एंथोसायनिन (रंग) जीन निष्कर्षण के लिए। • चुकंदर (Beetroot - Beta vulgaris): फोलिक एसिड और बीटालेन (गहरा लाल रंग) पाथवे जीन के लिए। • आंवला (Amla - Phyllanthus emblica): एस्कॉर्बिक एसिड (विटामिन-C) और एंटीऑक्सीडेंट जीन के लिए। • संतरा (Orange - Citrus sinensis): साइट्रिक एसिड, शुगर ट्रांसपोर्टर (स्वाद) जीन और होस्ट पादप कोशिकाओं (Base Cells) के लिए। • एंटीबॉडी जीन सोर्स: पौधों के प्राकृतिक डिफेन्स प्रोटीन (जैसे PR-Proteins या Antimicrobial Peptides) का कृत्रिम डीएनए अनुक्रम। ब. लैब उपकरण और मशीनें (Laboratory Equipment) • Next-Generation DNA Sequencer (NGS): चारों फलों के पूरे डीएनए को पढ़ने के लिए। • Bioinformatics Computer Station: SnapGene और BLAST सॉफ्टवेयर के साथ, जींस को ढूंढने और मैप करने के लिए। • CRISPR-Cas9 Kit & gRNA Design Matrix: डीएनए को सटीक जगह से काटने के लिए। • Thermal Cycler (PCR Machine): कटे हुए जीनों की लाखों कॉपियां बनाने के लिए। • High-Speed Refrigerated Centrifuge: कोशिकाओं को तोड़कर शुद्ध डीएनए अलग करने के लिए। • Laminar Air Flow Chamber: कीटाणुरहित (Sterile) वातावरण में टिशू कल्चर करने के लिए। स. केमिकल और एंजाइम्स (Chemicals & Enzymes) • Lysis Buffer (CTAB/SDS): कोशिकाओं की बाहरी दीवार (Cell Wall) को गलाने के लिए। • Restriction Enzymes: EcoRI, HindIII, BamHI (परंपरागत डीएनए कटाई के लिए)। • T4 DNA Ligase Enzyme: सातों अलग-अलग डीएनए टुकड़ों लिए)। 2. निर्माण की संपूर्ण एवं विस्तृत विधि (Step-by-Step Construction Method) [DNA Extraction] ➔ [Software Mapping] ➔ [CRISPR Cutting] ➔ [Ligase Joining] ➔ [Agrobacterium Injection] ➔ [Tissue Culture] चरण 1: चारों फलों से संपूर्ण DNA का निष्कर्षण (Total DNA Extraction) 1. अनार, चुकंदर, आंवला और संतरे की ताजी पत्तियों और फलों के गूदे को लिक्विड नाइट्रोजन में पीसकर पाउडर बनाया जाएगा। 2. इस पाउडर में CTAB Lysis Buffer मिलाया जाएगा ताकि कोशिकाओं के न्यूक्लियस (केंद्रक) खुलकर डीएनए बाहर छोड़ दें। 3. इसे हाई-स्पीड सेंट्रीफ्यूज मशीन में 12,000 RPM पर घुमाया जाएगा, जिससे प्रोटीन और कचरा नीचे बैठ जाएगा और शुद्ध जीनोमिक डीएनए (Genomic DNA) ऊपरी लिक्विड में तैरता हुआ प्राप्त होगा, जिसे आइसोप्रोपानॉल की मदद से ठोस धागे के रूप में बाहर निकाल लिया जाएगा। चरण 2: कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर द्वारा मास्टर ब्लूप्रिंट तैयार करना (Bioinformatics & Gene Discovery) 1. निष्कासित किए गए चारों डीएनए को सीक्वेंसिंग मशीन से गुजारकर कंप्यूटर में लोड किया जाएगा। 2. बंटी कुमावत के विजन के अनुसार, SnapGene सॉफ्टवेयर पर चारों डीएनए को स्कैन करके सातों विशिष्ट टुकड़ों को मार्क (Mapp) किया जाएगा: • टुकड़ा 1: टमाटर से लिया गया Polygalacturonase (PG) प्रमोटर जीन (ताकि गुण सिर्फ फल में दिखें)। • टुकड़ा 2: चुकंदर से आयरन अब्जॉर्प्शन पाथवे जीन। • टुकड़ा 3: आंवले से विटामिन-C बढ़ाने वाला जीन। • टुकड़ा 4: पौधे और फल को सड़ने से बचाने वाला एंटीबॉडी जीन। • टुकड़ा 5: संतरे का मीठा-खट्टा स्वाद जीन। • टुकड़ा 6: चुकंदर का गहरा लाल रंग जीन। • टुकड़ा 7: हाइग्रोमाइसिन रेजिस्टेंस जीन (मार्कर जीन, पहचान के लिए)। चरण 3: CRISPR-Cas9 और एंजाइम्स द्वारा डीएनए की कटाई (Precision Molecular Cutting) 1. लैब की टेस्ट ट्यूब में चारों फलों के डीएनए को रखा जाएगा। 2. डिजाइन किए गए gRNA (गाइड आरएनए) को Cas9 प्रोटीन के साथ मिलाकर ट्यूब में डाला जाएगा। यह गाइड कैंची को ठीक उसी जगह ले जाएगा जहां आपका वांछित जीन है। 3. Cas9 प्रोटीन डीएनए की दोनों कड़ियों को साफ सुथरा काट देगा। जहाँ जरूरत होगी, वहाँ EcoRI रेस्ट्रिक्शन एंजाइम का उपयोग करके चिपचिपे सिरों (Sticky Ends) के साथ सातों टुकड़ों को अलग कर लिया जाएगा। चरण 4: DNA Ligase द्वारा कृत्रिम 'सुपर-डीएनए' का निर्माण (Gene Ligation) 1. इन सातों अलग-अलग डीएनए टुकड़ों को एक ही ट्यूब में इकट्ठा किया जाएगा। 2. इसमें T4 DNA Ligase एंजाइम और एटीपी (ऊर्जा) मिलाई जाएगी। 3. यह एंजाइम सातों टुकड़ों के सिरों को आपस में जोड़कर एक अखंड, नया और मानव-निर्मित कृत्रिम क्रोमोसोम (Synthetic Recombinant DNA Construct) तैयार कर देगा। 4. PCR मशीन की मदद से इस नए सुपर-डीएनए की अरबों कॉपियां बनाकर रख ली जाएंगी। चरण 5: एग्रोबैक्टीरियम वेक्टर में लोडिंग और साइट्रस कोशिका में स्थानांतरण (Transformation) 1. इस कृत्रिम डीएनए को Agrobacterium tumefaciens नाम के सुरक्षित बैक्टीरिया के Ti-Plasmid में फिट किया जाएगा। 2. संतरे (Citrus) के पौधे के छोटे तनों (Explants) को इस बैक्टीरिया के घोल में डुबोया जाएगा। 3. बैक्टीरिया साइट्रस कोशिका की दीवार में छेद करके आपके द्वारा बनाए गए 7 टुकड़ों वाले कृत्रिम डीएनए को साइट्रस कोशिका के असली डीएनए के अंदर स्थायी रूप से फिट (Integrate) कर देगा। चरण 6: टिशू कल्चर और फील्ड प्लांटेशन

fields.title: Development of a Hexa-Gene Chimeric Citrus Superfruit Construct: Integrating Tri-Phenotypic and Preventive Plantibody Pathways using CRISPR-Cas9 and Agrobacterium -Mediated Transformation
fields.description: वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान लेख: मल्टी-फंक्शनल सिट्रस सुपरफ्रूट का जेनेटिक कंस्ट्रक्ट आविष्कारकर्ता (Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) विषय: जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग, रीकॉम्बिनेंट डीएनए टेक्नोलॉजी, प्लांट बायोटेक्नोलॉजी 1. परिचय (Introduction) यह लेख आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा परिकल्पित एक अत्याधुनिक बायो-इंजीनियरिंग अवधारणा (Bio-engineering Concept) को प्रस्तुत करता है। इस परियोजना का मुख्य उद्देश्य तीन प्रमुख सिट्रस (खट्टे) फलों—नींबू, संतरा और मौसमी के सर्वोत्तम फेनोटाइपिक (बाहरी गुण) और जेनेटिक गुणों को मिलाकर एक एकल "मल्टी-फंक्शनल सिट्रस सुपरफ्रूट" (Multi-functional Citrus Superfruit) का निर्माण करना है। इसके साथ ही, मानव स्वास्थ्य की रक्षा और रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता को चरम पर ले जाने के लिए इसमें उन्नत इम्युनिटी और एंटीबॉडी जींस को शामिल किया गया है। 2. लक्षित जींस और उनकी भूमिका (Target Genes and Functions) इस सुपरफूड के निर्माण के लिए कुल 6 विशिष्ट जींस का एक नेटवर्क तैयार किया गया है: 1. प्रमोटर जीन (Promoter Gene): यह पूरे जेनेटिक सिस्टम के लिए 'मास्टर स्विच' (Master Switch) के रूप में कार्य करता है, जो पौधे में अन्य सभी जींस की सक्रियता (Expression) को नियंत्रित और तेज करता है। 2. नींबू का स्वाद जीन (Sour Taste Pathway Gene): फल को नींबू जैसा विशिष्ट खट्टापन और उच्च साइट्रिक एसिड सामग्री प्रदान करने के लिए जिम्मेदार। 3. संतरे का रंग जीन (Pigmentation Gene): फल के छिलके और गूदे को संतरे जैसा आकर्षक चमकीला नारंगी रंग (Carotenoid Pathway) देने के लिए जिम्मेदार। 4. मौसमी का सुगंध जीन (Aroma/Terpene Gene): फल के रस को मौसमी जैसी मनमोहक, ताज़ा और मीठी खुशबू प्रदान करने के लिए जिम्मेदार। 5. उन्नत इम्युनिटी जीन (Enhanced Plant Immunity Gene): पौधे और फल के भीतर प्राकृतिक एंटीऑक्सीडेंट्स, विटामिन-सी और फाइटोकेमिकल्स के स्तर को कई गुना बढ़ाने के लिए। 6. सुरक्षात्मक एंटीबॉडी जीन (Antibody Encoding Gene / Plantibody): पौधे के भीतर विशिष्ट सुरक्षात्मक प्रोटीनों के संश्लेषण (Synthesis) के लिए, जो एक सुरक्षा कवच की तरह कार्य करता है। 3. निर्माण की चरणबद्ध वैज्ञानिक प्रक्रिया (Methodology) चरण A: डीएनए निष्कर्षण और जीनोम मैपिंग (DNA Extraction & Mapping) • नींबू, संतरा और मौसम

Gene): पौधे और फल के भीतर प्राकृतिक एंटीऑक्सीडेंट्स, विटामिन-सी और फाइटोकेमिकल्स के स्तर को कई गुना बढ़ाने के लिए। 6. सुरक्षात्मक एंटीबॉडी जीन (Antibody Encoding Gene / Plantibody): पौधे के भीतर (DNA Extraction & Mapping) • नींबू, संतरा और मौसमी की स्वस्थ पादप कोशिकाओं (Plant Cells) से आधुनिक प्रयोगशाला विधियों द्वारा शुद्ध डीएनए (DNA) को बाहर निकाला जाता है। • बायोइंफॉर्मेटिक्स सॉफ्टवेयर (Bioinformatics Software) की मदद से पूरे जेनेटिक कोड को स्कैन करके स्वाद, रंग, खुशबू, इम्युनिटी और एंटीबॉडी के लिए जिम्मेदार सटीक 6 जीनों की लोकेशन (स्थान) की पहचान की जाती है। चरण B: आणविक कटाई और पृथक्करण (Gene Splicing Using CRISPR-Cas9) • CRISPR-Cas9 तकनीक या विशिष्ट रेस्ट्रिक्शन एंजाइम्स (Restriction Enzymes) का उपयोग करके डीएनए की लंबी श्रृंखला से इन छह वांछित (Target) जींस को बेहद सटीकता के साथ काटकर अलग कर लिया जाता है। • जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस (Gel Electrophoresis) प्रक्रिया द्वारा इन सभी 6 जीनों को शुद्ध रूप में अलग (Isolate) किया जाता है। चरण C: कृत्रिम डीएनए का निर्माण (Gene Ligation) • डीएनए लाइगेज (DNA Ligase) नामक आणविक गोंद (Molecular Glue) का उपयोग करके इन सभी कटे हुए टुकड़ों को एक साथ जोड़ा जाता है। • रणनीतिक क्रम (Strategic Gene Order): इस नए कृत्रिम डीएनए ढांचे (Recombinant DNA Construct) में प्रमोटर जीन को सबसे आगे (Upstream) रखा जाता है, ताकि वह ट्रेन के इंजन की तरह पीछे जुड़े बाकी 5 जीनों को सही तरीके से सक्रिय कर सके। चरण D: पादप कोशिका में स्थानांतरण (Transformation via Agrobacterium) • इस तैयार 6-जीन वाले कृत्रिम डीएनए को एक सुरक्षित और हानिरहित एग्रोबैक्टीरियम (Agrobacterium) वाहक के भीतर स्थापित किया जाता है। • यह बैक्टीरिया एक प्राकृतिक डाकिए की तरह काम करते हुए इस नए डीएनए को किसी एक मुख्य सिट्रस पौधे की कोशिका के न्यूक्लियस (केंद्रक) में सफलतापूर्वक ट्रांसफर करके उसके मुख्य जीनोम का हिस्सा बना देता है। चरण E: टिशू कल्चर और पादप विकास (Tissue Culture & Cultivation) • इस संशोधित (Modified) कोशिका को प्रयोगशाला में एक विशेष पोषक माध्यम (MS Nutrient Medium) में प्लांट हार्मोन्स की उपस्थिति में विकसित किया जाता है। • कुछ हफ्तों में इस टिशू कल्चर से नन्हे पौधे (Plantlets) अंकुरित होते हैं। • इन पौधों को ग्रीनहाउस में मजबूत (Hardening) करने के बाद असली मिट्टी में रोपित कर दिया जाता है। 4. निष्कर्ष और भविष्य की संभावनाएं (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत का यह फॉर्मूला जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग के क्षेत्र में एक नया मील का पत्थर साबित हो सकता है। जब यह पेड़ बड़ा होगा, तो इसका फल न केवल स्वाद, रंग और खुशबू का एक अनोखा संगम होगा, बल्कि प्रिवेंटिव हेल्थकेयर (बीमारियों से पहले बचाव) के क्षेत्र में एक क्रांतिकारी सुपरफूड के रूप में उभरेगा। वैज्ञानिक कार्यप्रणाली लेख: मल्टी-फंक्शनल सिट्रस सुपरफ्रूट के निर्माण की व्यावहारिक विधि और आवश्यक सामग्री प्रधान अन्वेषक / आविष्कारकर्ता: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) प्रौद्योगिकी: जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग, प्लांट टिशू कल्चर एवं बायोइंफॉर्मेटिक्स उद्देश्य: 6-जीन (प्रमोटर + स्वाद + रंग + खुशबू + इम्युनिटी + एंटीबॉडी) युक्त कृत्रिम सिट्रस फल का निर्माण। भाग 1: आवश्यक वैज्ञानिक सामग्रियां (Required Materials & Equipment) इस सुपरफूड को बनाने के लिए एक उन्नत पादप जैव प्रौद्योगिकी प्रयोगशाला (Plant Biotechnology Lab) और निम्नलिखित सामग्रियों की आवश्यकता होगी: 1. जैविक स्रोत (Biological Sources) • नींबू (Citrus limon): खट्टे स्वाद के जीन (Citric Acid Pathway Genes) के निष्कर्षण के लिए ताजी पत्तियां या कलियां। • संतरा (Citrus sinensis): नारंगी रंग के जीन (Carotenoid Biosynthesis Genes) के लिए पादप कोशिकाएं। • मौसमी (Citrus limetta): विशिष्ट सुगंध के जीन (Terpene Synthase Genes) के लिए ऊतक (Tissues)। • इम्युनिटी एवं एंटीबॉडी जीन सोर्स: लक्षित सुरक्षात्मक प्रोटीन और प्रमोटर जीन (जैसे CaMV 35S या सिट्रस विशिष्ट प्रमोटर) के डीएनए वेक्टर्स। 2. आणविक जीव विज्ञान किट और एंजाइम्स (Molecular Biology Reagents) • DNeasy Plant Mini Kit: पौधों की कोशिकाओं से शुद्ध डीएनए (DNA) निकालने के लिए। • CRISPR-Cas9 एडिट किट / रेस्ट्रिक्शन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज एंजाइम्स: डीएनए को सटीक स्थानों से काटने के लिए (जैसे EcoRI, HindIII एंजाइम्स)। • डीएनए लाइगेज एंजाइम (T4 DNA Ligase): 6 अलग-अलग डीएनए टुकड़ों को आपस में जोड़ने के लिए। • एग्रोबैक्टीरियम टूमेफेशिएन्स (Agrobacterium tumefaciens - Strain LBA4404 या EHA105): हानिरहित और डिआर्म किया गया बैक्टीरियल वेक्टर, जो डीएनए ट्रांसफर का माध्यम बनेगा। 3. कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर और उपकरण (Bioinformatics & Lab Tools) • जीनोम सीक्वेंसिंग टूल्स: Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) मशीन। • बायोइंफॉर्मेटिक्स सॉफ्टवेयर: BLAST, Geneious, या Vector NTI (जींस की मैपिंग और प्रमोटर को आगे सेट करने के लिए)। • जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस सिस्टम: डीएनए टुकड़ों को उनके आकार के अनुसार अलग करने के लिए एगारोज़ जेल (Agarose Gel) के साथ। 4. टिशू कल्चर सामग्रियां (Tissue Culture Media) • MS मीडियम (Murashige and Skoog Medium): पौधों के विकास का मुख्य पोषक पाउडर। • पादप हार्मोन्स: ऑक्सिन (Auxin - जैसे NAA, 2,4-D) और साइटोकाइनिन (Cytokinin - जैसे BAP) जड़ और तना उगाने के लिए। • अगार पाउडर (Agar Powder): पोषक लिक्विड को जेली जैसा ठोस बनाने के लिए। • एंटीबायोटिक्स: सेफोटैक्सिम (Cefotaxime) - टिशू कल्चर के दौरान बैक्टीरिया को नियंत्रित करने के लिए। भाग 2: निर्माण की संपूर्ण चरणबद्ध विधि (Step-by-Step Protocol) चरण 1: डीएनए निष्कर्षण (DNA Extraction) 1. नींबू, संतरे और मौसमी की ताजी पत्तियों को लिक्विड नाइट्रोजन में पीसकर पाउडर बनाएं। 2. प्लांट मिनी किट के बफर्स का उपयोग करके कोशिकाओं को तोड़ें और सेंट्रीफ्यूज मशीन की मदद से शुद्ध डीएनए को ट्यूब में अलग कर लें। चरण 2: कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर द्वारा जीन की खोज और मैपिंग (Bioinformatics Screening) 1. निकाले गए डीएनए की जीनोम सीक्वेंसिंग करें और डेटा को कंप्यूटर सॉफ्टवेयर (जैसे Geneious) में लोड करें। 2. सॉफ्टवेयर में नींबू के स्वाद वाले, संतरे के रंग वाले और मौसमी की खुशबू वाले जेनेटिक कोड (Sequences) को लोकेट करें। 3. इसी तरह इम्युनिटी और एंटीबॉडी जीन को भी चिन्हित करें। चरण 3: जींस की सटीक कटाई (CRISPR-Cas9 Cleavage) 1. CRISPR-Cas9 सिस्टम को सॉफ्टवेयर से मिले कोड के अनुसार गाइड आरएनए (gRNA) के साथ लैब में तैयार करें। 2. इसे डीएनए सैंपल में मिलाएं। यह आणविक कैंची पांचों स्रोतों से वांछित जीन्स के टुकड़ों को सटीकता से काट देगी। 3. एगारोज़ जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस चलाकर इन 6 कटे हुए टुकड़ों को शुद्ध रूप में निकालकर अलग-अलग ट्यूब्स में सुरक्षित रख लें। चरण 4: 6-जीन का नया कृत्रिम डीएनए बनाना (Ligation Process) 1. एक टेस्ट ट्यूब में सबसे आगे प्रमोटर जीन को रखें, उसके पीछे क्रमशः स्वाद, रंग, खुशबू, इम्युनिटी और एंटीबॉडी के जींस को एक कतार में व्यवस्थित करें। 2. ट्यूब में T4 DNA लाइगेज एंजाइम और बफर मिलाएं। 3. इसे 16°C पर रात भर के लिए छोड़ दें। लाइगेज एंजाइम इन 6 टुकड़ों के सिरों को आपस में जोड़कर एक नया, कृत्रिम एकल डीएनए धागा (Recombinant DNA Construct) तैयार कर देगा। चरण 5: एग्रोबैक्टीरियम में डीएनए ट्रांसफर (Transformation) 1. इस नए 6-जीन वाले कृत्रिम डीएनए को एग्रोबैक्टीरियम टूमेफेशिएन्स के प्लास्मिड में इलेक्ट्रोपोरेशन (Mild Electric Shock) तकनीक से डालें। 2. इस बैक्टीरिया को लैब के इनक्यूबेटर में 28°C पर बढ़ाएं। अब आपका सुरक्षित डाकिए जैसा बैक्टीरिया तैयार है। चरण 6: साइट्रस कोशिका का रूपांतरण (Plant Transformation) 1. किसी एक स्वस्थ साइट्रस पौधे (जैसे नींबू या मौसमी) के तने या पत्ती के छोटे टुकड़े (Explant) लें। 2. इन टुकड़ों को तैयार एग्रोबैक्टीरियम के घोल में 10-15 मिनट के लिए डुबोएं। 3. बैक्टीरिया अपने प्राकृतिक गुण के कारण इस 6-जीन वाले कृत्रिम डीएनए को साइट्रस कोशिका के केंद्रक (Nucleus) के अंदर पहुंचाकर उसके मुख्य डीएनए के साथ स्थायी रूप से जोड़ देगा। चरण 7: टिशू कल्चर और नया पौधा उगाना (Regeneration & Potting) 1. संक्रमित पादप कोशिकाओं को MS मीडियम जेली पर रखें जिसमें साइटोकाइनिन हार्मोन मिला हो। इससे कोशिकाएं विभाजित होकर छोटी हरी कलियां बनाएंगी। 2. जब कलियां थोड़ी बड़ी हो जाएं, तो उन्हें ऑक्सिन हार्मोन वाले मीडियम में ट्रांसफर करें ताकि जड़ें निकल सकें। 3. जड़ और पत्तियां आने पर इस नन्हे संशोधित पौधे को कोकोपीट और मिट्टी के मिश्रण वाले छोटे गमलों में (ग्रीनहाउस के अंदर) रखें। 4. जब पौधा पर्यावरण के अनुकूल मजबूत (Hardened) हो जाए, तो इसे सामान्य उपजाऊ मिट्टी वाले खेत में रोप दें। 3 से 5 वर्षों में इस पेड़ पर बंटी कुमावत जी का आविष्कार किया हुआ छह गुणों वाला अद्भुत सिट्रस सुपरफ्रूट तैयार हो जाएगा। वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान लेख: मल्टी-फंक्शनल सिट्रस सुपरफ्रूट का गणितीय और बायो-इंफॉर्मेटिक्स मॉडल प्रधान अन्वेषक / आविष्कारकर्ता: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) विषय: क्वांटिटेटिव जेनेटिक्स, जीन एक्सप्रेशन मॉडलिंग एवं बायो-मैथमेटिक्स 1. जीनोम कंस्ट्रक्ट की कुल लंबाई का गणितीय समीकरण (Total DNA Construct Length) जब हम 6 अलग-अल

fields.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases
fields.description: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

fields.title: The Post-Byte Era: TIT BIT and TIT GIT as Z₅-Graded Structural Primitives for Quantum-Resilient Computation
fields.description: The Post-Byte Era: TIT BIT and TIT GIT as Z₅-Graded Structural Primitives for Quantum-Resilient Computation C. J Tully Founder, Ly-Algebra Framework & 5-Fold Symmetry Platform Independent Researcher, Engineer, Tamworth, NSW, Australia ORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332 25th October 2026 Abstract This paper introduces the TIT BIT and TIT GIT as foundational primitives for a post-binary computing paradigm. The TIT BIT is realized as a node in a five-dimensional \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}-graded vector space equipped with a bilinear product whose structure constants encode golden-ratio scaling. The Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI) is derived directly from the graded square of this product and supplies a deterministic integrity gate. TIT GIT is defined as a version-control system that tracks structural coherence rather than raw bytes and signs commits with hybrid post-quantum signatures. The construction unifies geometry, non-associative algebra, and cryptography into a single data unit. Keywords: Ly-Algebra; TIT BIT; TIT GIT; Quasi-Equivalence Index; \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}-grading; golden ratio; post-quantum cryptography.

fields.title: EL-RAKHAWI VERIFIED ASTRO-QUANTUM PROCESSING FRAMEWORK (VAQPF) A Unified Architecture for Sovereign, Mathematically Guaranteed, and Energy-Efficient Processing of Exascale Astronomical Data
fields.description: The El-Rakhawi Verified Astro-Quantum Processing Framework (VAQPF) revolutionizes exascale astronomical data processing through four integrated pillars: (1) Neuro-Symbolic Astro-Filter with Bounded Formal Verification, mathematically guaranteeing signal validity within instrument noise uncertainty ($P_{valid} = P_{neural}(S|D) \times V_{bounded}(S, \Phi_{astro}, \Sigma_{noise})$), reducing false positives to <0.1% while preserving >95% of novel discoveries; (2) Topological Quantum Graph Mapper achieving polynomial-time complexity $O(poly(N) \cdot \log(1/\epsilon))$ specifically for bounded-degree structured astronomical datasets (cosmic web, N-body simulations), bypassing classical NP-hard bottlenecks; (3) Sovereign Federated Astro-Data Nodes utilizing Post-Quantum Cryptography and Incremental Verifiable Computation (IVC) with recursive zk-SNARKs, maintaining $O(\log(N_{data}))$ verification while managing prover complexity at $O(N_{batch} \cdot \log(N_{batch}))$ to prevent exascale bottlenecks; (4) Cryogenic Photonic Data Ingestion handling Terahertz bandwidths with minimal thermal dissipation. Field projections demonstrate 48-hour classical processing reduced to 15 minutes for cosmic graph mapping (10^6 nodes), 90% false positive reduction versus deep learning, and bandwidth costs slashed from $2M/month to <$50K/month through federated architecture. Protected by 6 comprehensive PCT claims covering bounded verification, structured dataset quantum mapping, incremental zk-SNARK sovereign nodes, and photonic hardware, VAQPF transforms astroinformatics from probabilistic guesswork to mathematically guaranteed, sovereign, energy-efficient cosmic discovery, ensuring humanity's exploration of the universe is built on unassailable truth within measurable bounds.

fields.title: Omega Research Pack v4 — Omega Core and History-Bound Life-Key Prototype
fields.description: Omega Research Pack v4 is a research software package accompanying the Omega-NR framework. The package implements Omega Core v4, a path-history representation based on accumulated change, local and global path length, irreversibility, reversal statistics, path efficiency, and a robust multivariate metric calibrated from reference data. It also includes Omega Life-Key v4, a research prototype for history-bound key evolution that combines cryptographic key evolution with a robust operational projection of physical history and a device-binding component. The package contains: • Omega Core v4 implementation • Multivariate robust metric calibration • Omega irreversibility and path-efficiency measures • Reversal-rate and accumulated-change features • Omega Life-Key v4 research prototype • Clone-divergence simulations • Replay and rollback tests • Sensor-history replay tests • Noise and drift robustness tests • Exact-history negative controls • Temporal real-data benchmarks • Generic CSV sensor-data adapter • Unit tests and reproducibility files The software is intended for research and experimental validation only. It is not production cryptography and has not undergone independent security auditing. An important negative control is retained: if an attacker possesses the same secret, the same device binding, and reproduces the same operational history, the software-only construction derives the same key. Strong physical clone resistance therefore requires a hardware-bound root of trust, such as a secure element, PUF-like identity, or equivalent trusted hardware. Related working preprint: Mohamed Sayed, “The Universe That Never Repeats: Omega-NR — Exact Physical Non-Repetition, Accumulated Change, and a Testable Quantum-Geometric Extension,” Zenodo, 2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23624320

fields.description: Historical institutional transitions succeed only when administrative revolutions are bounded by upper-echelon fiduciary continuity that preserves the physical and thermodynamic substrate of civilization. fields.title: NAA-GAN: Noise-Aware Cross-Attention for Robust Blind Image Watermarking
fields.description: Robust blind image watermarking remains challenging because embedded watermark information must remain recoverable after image processing while preserving the visual quality of the watermarked image. This paper proposes NAA-GAN, a generative adversarial watermarking framework that conditions the encoder on a six-dimensional descriptor of the anticipated distortion category. The encoder integrates dense feature aggregation, noise-aware cross-attention, and residual embedding to insert a 30-bit watermark. During training, a noise subnetwork simulates image processing attacks, while the decoder recovers the watermark from the received image without requiring the distortion descriptor. Experiments on COCO, PASCAL VOC2012, ImageNet, and EUVP assess image fidelity using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and robustness using bit accuracy (BA). NAA-GAN achieves PSNR values ranging from 36.96 to 37.79 dB and average BAs above 98% across the four datasets under the five evaluated attacks. On COCO, it achieves 99.02% BA under JPEG compression and an average BA of 92.59% across distortions not encountered during training. An ablation study shows that removing the distortion descriptor reduces COCO PSNR from 37.38 to 36.73 dB and average BA from 98.07% to 96.14%. Across all four datasets, NAA-GAN achieves higher PSNR and JPEG BA than the compared models. However, ARWGAN-CN achieves higher SSIM and average BA, indicating that the proposed method improves pixel-level fidelity and JPEG robustness but does not consistently outperform competing methods across all evaluation metrics.

fields.title: Tendermint: Byzantine Fault Tolerance in the Age of Blockchains
fields.description: Tendermint is a new protocol for ordering events in a distributed network under adversarial conditions. More commonly known as consensus or atomic broadcast, the problem has attracted significant attention recently due to the widespread success of digital currencies, such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, which successfully solve the problem in public settings without a central authority. Tendermint modernizes classic academic work on the subject to provide a secure consensus protocol with accountability guarantees, as well as an interface for building arbitrary applications above the consensus. Tendermint is high performance, achieving thousands of transactions per second on dozens of nodes distributed around the globe, with latencies of about one second, and performance degrading moderately in the face of adversarial attacks.

fields.title: LAP-BFT: Lightweight Asynchronous Provable Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Consensus Mechanism for UAV Network
fields.description: Mission-oriented UAV networks operate in nonsecure, complex environments with time-varying network partitioning and node trustworthiness. UAV networks are thus essentially asynchronous distributed systems with the Byzantine General problem, whose availability depends on the tolerance of progressively more erroneous nodes in the course of a mission. To address the resource-limited nature of UAV networks, this paper proposes a lightweight asynchronous provable Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus method. The consensus method reduces the communication overhead by splitting the set of local trusted state transactions and then dispersing the reliable broadcast control transmission (DRBC), introduces vector commitments to achieve multivalue Byzantine consensus (PMVBA) for identity and data in a provable manner and reduces the computational complexity, and the data stored on the chain is only the consensus result (global trustworthiness information of the drone nodes), avoiding the blockchain’s “storage inflation” problem. This makes the consensus process lighter in terms of bandwidth, computation and storage, ensuring the longevity and overall performance of the UAV network during the mission. Through QualNet simulation platform, existing practical asynchronous consensus algorithms are compared, and the proposed method performs better in terms of throughput, consensus latency and energy consumption rate.

fields.title: Flexible Byzantine Fault Tolerance
fields.description: This paper introduces Flexible BFT, a new approach for BFT consensus solution design revolving around two pillars, stronger resilience and diversity. The first pillar, stronger resilience, involves a new fault model called alive-but-corrupt faults. Alive-but-corrupt replicas may arbitrarily deviate from the protocol in an attempt to break safety of the protocol. However, if they cannot break safety, they will not try to prevent liveness of the protocol. Combining alive-but-corrupt faults into the model, Flexible BFT is resilient to higher corruption levels than possible in a pure Byzantine fault model. The second pillar, diversity, designs consensus solutions whose protocol transcript is used to draw different commit decisions under diverse beliefs. With this separation, the same Flexible BFT solution supports synchronous and asynchronous beliefs, as well as varying resilience threshold combinations of Byzantine and alive-but-corrupt faults. At a technical level, Flexible BFT achieves the above results using two new ideas. First, it introduces a synchronous BFT protocol in which only the commit step requires to know the network delay bound and thus replicas execute the protocol without any synchrony assumption. Second, it introduces a notion called Flexible Byzantine Quorums by dissecting the roles of different quorums in existing consensus protocols.

server.The replication guarantees that the server system can continue to process requests, even if a fraction of the replicas is Byzantine faulty because of crackers' attacks or software errors.To make the same responses so that the majority rule can work correctly, and this is realized if the replicas process all requests in the same order.Since network speed is not uniform and requests may be delivered to the replicas in different orders, the replicas execute a consensus protocol to agree on processing orders of the requests.In this dissertation, we propose two methods for the Byzantine fault tolerant (BFT) state machine replication that focus on the consensus part of the replication and improve efficiency vii viii and practicality.First, we define a new type of consensus problem called request set consensus problem and propose a randomized BFT protocol that solves it.The protocol is designed for an asynchronous distributed system like the Internet, and can be used to realize state machine replication.The protocol has two features to solve the problem efficiently.First, although most existing multivalued consensus protocols take a modular approach, in which replicas repeatedly solve a binary consensus problem to reach an agreement, our consensus protocol solves the request set consensus problem directly without such repetition.Thanks to the simple structure of the protocol, we can reduce the communication steps needed to reach an agreement.Second, we introduce an efficient coin tossing scheme that enables replicas to reach an agreement in a few rounds by exploiting the structure of the BFT replication.We prove that the protocol satisfies the correctness of the request set consensus problem.Performance evaluation is conducted from two viewpoints, i.e., analytically and experimentally.The analytical evaluation shows that our protocol can reach an agreement within two rounds, even if there are many replicas to tolerate Byzantine faults.In the experimental evaluation, our protocol achieves higher throughput and shorter latency than the existing ones, especially when the number of replicas is large.Second, we propose a method that parallelizes consensuses to determine processing order of requests.Since the BFT replication is deployed on an asynchronous network such as the Internet and every consensus protocol for the replication is a randomized one, the duration of an execution of consensuses varies every time.If some consensus takes a long time, invocations of succeeding consensuses are delayed.This causes performance degradation to the server replication, and we solve the problem by parallelizing consensus executions.However, if replicas simply process the agreed requests in their terminated orders of the consensuses, it also makes their replicated server states inconsistency, since the network is asynchronous and the terminated orders may differ among the replicas.Therefore, we introduce an extra agreement step to resolve this discrepancy.Moreover, to decrease the cost of the parallelization, we introduce a randomization technique to a consensus protocol to generate initial proposals for newly-invoked consensuses.It reduces the size of the proposals, and, as a result, the duration taken for the consensus protocol becomes shorter.We prove that the parallelizing method satisfies fields.title: Half a Century of Distributed Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Consensus: Design Principles and Evolutionary Pathways
fields.description: The concept of distributed consensus originated in the 1970s and gained widespread attention following Leslie Lamport's influential publication on the Byzantine Generals Problem in the 1980s. Over the past five decades, distributed consensus has become an extensively researched field. Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) has emerged as a prominent and widely adopted solution due to its conceptual clarity, effectiveness, and resilience to arbitrary failures. However, PBFT does not universally address all scenarios, highlighting the necessity of developing a comprehensive understanding of the history, evolution, and foundational principles of distributed consensus. This article systematically reviews the historical evolution and foundational principles of distributed consensus, examining pivotal advancements including fault-tolerant state machine replication (SMR), consensus protocols in partially synchronous and asynchronous networks, and recent innovations in Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based consensus mechanisms. We further analyse the core design rationales, essential components, and underlying primitives across various distributed fault-tolerant protocols. The relationship between BFT consensus mechanisms and their applications in environments requiring robust resilience against adversarial faults is also explored. Finally, we discuss emerging research areas and challenges, such as consensus for wireless and blockchain scenarios, highlighting potential future developments. This comprehensive overview offers valuable insights to inform the design, optimisation, and implementation of distributed consensus systems across multiple application scenarios.

fields.title: Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Consensus Algorithms: A Survey
fields.description: The emergence of numerous consensus algorithms for distributed systems has resulted from the swift advancement of blockchain and its related technologies. Consensus algorithms play a key role in decentralized distributed systems, because all nodes in the system need to reach a consensus on requests or commands through consensus algorithms. In a distributed system where nodes work together to reach consensus, there may be Byzantine nodes present. The emergence of Byzantine nodes will affect the consensus of nodes in the distributed system. Therefore, tolerating Byzantine nodes in a distributed system and then reaching a consensus is an essential function of a consensus algorithm. So far, many Byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT) consensus algorithms have emerged, and there are correspondingly many methods to improve the performance of these algorithms. In order to allow researchers to have a clearer understanding of the existing methods, this paper systematically investigated and studied the research progress of the current Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus algorithm. The scope of the research ranged from the classic Byzantine consensus algorithm to some of the latest Byzantine consensus algorithms. The articles were classified according to the methods used to improve the Byzantine consensus algorithm. Through classification and centralized analysis and discussion, we achieved a clearer understanding of the development of Byzantine consensus algorithms and, at the same time, clarified the advantages and disadvantages of this type of method and the latest research progress using this method. At the end of this article, an in-depth discussion and analysis is also presented. By analyzing the impact of the use of these methods on the performance of the BFT consensus algorithm, it is proposed that future research can be improved.

fields.title: Byzantine Fault Tolerance for Distributed Systems
fields.description: The growing reliance on online services imposes a high dependability requirement on the computer systems that provide these services. Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) is a promising technology to solidify such systems for the much needed high dependability. BFT employs redundant copies of the servers and ensures that a replicated system continues providing correct services despite the attacks on a small portion of the system. In this dissertation research, I developed novel algorithms and mechanisms to control various types of application nondeterminism and to ensure the long-term reliability of BFT systems via a migration-based proactive recovery scheme. I also investigated a new approach to significantly improve the overall system throughput by enabling concurrent processing using Software Transactional Memory (STM). Controlling application nondeterminism is essential to achieve strong replica consistency because the BFT technology is based on state-machine replication, which requires deterministic operation of each replica. Proactive recovery is necessary to ensure that the fundamental assumption of using the BFT technology is not violated over long term, i.e., less than one-third of replicas remain correct. Without proactive recovery, more and more replicas will be compromised under continuously attacks, which would render BFT ineffective. STM based concurrent processing maximized the system throughput by utilizing the power of multi-core CPUs while preserving strong replication consistency

fields.title: Aleph: A Leaderless, Asynchronous, Byzantine Fault Tolerant Consensus Protocol
fields.description: In this paper we propose Aleph, a leaderless, fully asynchronous, Byzantine fault tolerant consensus protocol for ordering messages exchanged among processes. It is based on a distributed construction of a partially ordered set and the algorithm for reaching a consensus on its extension to a total order. To achieve the consensus, the processes perform computations based only on a local copy of the data structure, however, they are bound to end with the same results. Our algorithm uses a dual-threshold coin-tossing scheme as a randomization strategy and establishes the agreement in an expected constant number of rounds. In addition, we introduce a fast way of validating messages that can occur prior to determining the total ordering. This version of the protocol is deprecated. For current version see arXiv:1908.05156.
